boghossian.what: A foundation created in 1992 by the jeweller Robert Boghossian and his sons Jean and Albert, of Armenian origin, based at the Villa Empain in Brussels.
boghossian.money: The Boghossian family of jewellers who created it.
boghossian.arts: In its first fifteen years it worked mainly on the living conditions of young people in Armenia and Lebanon.

bohemiasekt.name: Bohemia Sekt
bohemiasekt.what: A Czech sparkling wine maker in Starý Plzenec near Plzeň, producing sekt there since 1945; Germany's Henkell group took a qualified majority in the company in 1999.
bohemiasekt.money: Sales of its own sparkling wines and of Henkell Freixenet brands such as Freixenet cava and Mionetto prosecco on the Czech market.

bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.name: Bonnier AB
bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.what: A privately held Swedish group founded in 1804 by Gerhard Bonnier and controlled by the Bonnier family, with 175 companies in 15 countries.
bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.money: Media, real estate through Bonnier Fastigheter and investments through Bonnier Capital: EBITA of SEK 2,402 million in 2025.

bpd.name: BPD | Bouwfonds Gebiedsontwikkeling
bpd.what: A Dutch and German area developer founded in 1946 as Bouwspaarkas Drentsche Gemeenten, headquartered in Amsterdam and wholly owned by Rabobank.
bpd.money: Developing and selling homes and residential areas in the Netherlands and Germany, about 395,000 homes so far.
bpd.arts: Its BPD Cultuurfonds has funded art and culture projects tied to architecture and the built environment for over 35 years, and BPD owns over 1,000 contemporary artworks.

bradesco.name: Banco Bradesco S.A.
bradesco.what: A Brazilian bank founded by Amador Aguiar in Marília in 1943, headquartered at Cidade de Deus in Osasco, São Paulo state; Brazil's third largest bank by assets.
bradesco.money: Its commercial banking, insurance, pension, annuity and credit card business; revenue was US$35.3 billion in 2025.

bramall.name: The Liz and Terry Bramall Foundation
bramall.what: A grant-making charity (England and Wales number 1121670) set up by Terry Bramall, former chairman of the housebuilder Keepmoat, with a £100 million endowment in 2008.
bramall.money: Terry Bramall's fortune from Keepmoat, sold in 2007 for £783 million; the charity's investments earned £2.43 million in the year to 5 April 2025.
bramall.arts: Promoting the arts is one of its charitable purposes; it spent £7.76 million on charitable activities in the year to 5 April 2025.

brazilianforeignministry|Brazil.name: Ministério das Relações Exteriores
brazilianforeignministry|Brazil.what: Brazil's foreign ministry, called Itamaraty after the palace that houses it in Brasília, which advises the president on foreign relations; Mauro Vieira has been minister since January 2023.
brazilianforeignministry|Brazil.arts: Its remit includes the cultural side of Brazil's foreign relations.

brazilsministryofculture|Brazil.name: Ministério da Cultura
brazilsministryofculture|Brazil.what: Brazil's federal culture ministry, created in March 1985 under President José Sarney, abolished three times, most recently in 2019, and re-created on 1 January 2023 under Margareth Menezes.
brazilsministryofculture|Brazil.arts: Its main instrument is the Lei Rouanet of 1991, which lets companies and individuals sponsor culture against up to 4% and 6% of their income tax.

brdgroupesocitgnrale.name: BRD - Groupe Société Générale S.A.
brdgroupesocitgnrale.what: A Romanian bank based in Bucharest, formerly the state Banca Română pentru Dezvoltare, bought by France's Société Générale in 1999, which holds 60.17%.
brdgroupesocitgnrale.money: Commercial, investment and private banking in Romania, with revenue of RON 4.3 billion and net income of RON 1.5 billion in 2025.

brickworks.name: Brickworks Limited
brickworks.what: Australia's largest brick manufacturer and building products company, combined with the Sydney investment house Washington H. Soul Pattinson in September 2025.
brickworks.money: Sales of bricks and other building products in Australia and North America, plus industrial property and investments.

britishcolumbiaartscouncil|Canada.name: BC Arts Council
britishcolumbiaartscouncil|Canada.what: An agency of the Province of British Columbia, created in 1995 under the Arts Council Act and based in Victoria.
britishcolumbiaartscouncil|Canada.money: The provincial budget, through the Ministry of Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport.
britishcolumbiaartscouncil|Canada.address: 2nd Floor, 800 Johnson Street, Victoria, BC V8W 1N3

britishcouncil|UK.name: British Council
britishcouncil|UK.what: The UK's cultural relations organisation under royal charter, a public corporation and charity sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
britishcouncil|UK.money: Commercial income, 69 per cent of it from English teaching and exams in 2024-25, plus FCDO grant-in-aid of about 15 per cent.

britishcouncil|Ukraine.name: British Council
britishcouncil|Ukraine.what: The United Kingdom's charity for international cultural and educational relations, sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and working in over 100 countries.
britishcouncil|Ukraine.money: Mostly commercial income, 69 percent of its GBP 1.01 billion in 2024/25 from English teaching and exams; FCDO grant-in-aid gives about 15 percent.

britishfriendsofballetnacionaldecuba.name: The British Friends of Ballet Nacional de Cuba
britishfriendsofballetnacionaldecuba.what: A London charity registered on 7 October 2008, under a constitution adopted that February, to support the Ballet Nacional de Cuba.
britishfriendsofballetnacionaldecuba.money: Total income was £8,150 in the year to 31 December 2025.

brotfrdiwelt.name: Brot für die Welt
brotfrdiwelt.what: The worldwide aid agency of Germany's Protestant regional and free churches, part of the Evangelisches Werk für Diakonie und Entwicklung in Berlin.
brotfrdiwelt.money: Federal and church development funds plus donations; of EUR 341.7 million available in 2025, donations and collections gave EUR 72.6 million.

brown.name: The Brown Foundation, Inc.
brown.what: A Houston family foundation set up in 1951 by the brothers Herman and George R. Brown and their wives, Margarett Root Brown and Alice Pratt Brown.
brown.money: The Brown brothers' fortune from Brown & Root, the construction firm merged with Halliburton in 1962.
brown.arts: It has distributed more than US$2 billion since 1951, with arts and education among its five areas.

brownforman.name: Brown-Forman Corporation
brownforman.what: A family-controlled, publicly traded US spirits and wine company, maker of Jack Daniel's and Woodford Reserve, founded in Louisville, Kentucky, in 1870 by George Garvin Brown.
brownforman.money: Sales of its spirits and wines: revenue of USD 5.37 billion and net income of USD 783 million in the year to April 2025.

brusselscapital.name: Brussels-Capital Region
brusselscapital.what: One of the three federal regions of Belgium, formed on 18 June 1989; its government is a minister-president and four ministers elected by the regional parliament.
brusselscapital.money: The regional budget, voted by the Brussels Parliament; the government's 2026 budget closes with a deficit of 957 million euros.

bruzz.name: Vlaams-Brusselse Media vzw
bruzz.what: A non-profit media company founded in 2014 for the Flemish community in Brussels; Bruzz, its brand since 2016, works from the Flagey building in Ixelles.
bruzz.money: It works under a management agreement with the Flemish Community and the Flemish Community Commission (VGC).
bruzz.wrong_match: Bruzz is a Brussels news outlet that Beursschouwburg lists under financial support and sponsors, and no page opened shows it giving money rather than media space.

bukhman.name: Bukhman Foundation
bukhman.what: A London charity (no. 1205571) set up in 2023 by Igor and Anastasia Bukhman; Igor co-founded the mobile games company Playrix with his brother Dmitry in 2004.
bukhman.money: Donations, £2.55 million of £2.57 million income in the year to March 2025; Igor Bukhman's fortune comes from Playrix.

bulgari.name: Bulgari S.p.A.
bulgari.what: An Italian luxury house founded in Rome in 1884 by the silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris, owned by the French group LVMH since 2011.
bulgari.money: Sales of jewellery, watches, fragrances, accessories and leather goods, as part of LVMH.

bundesministeriumfrkunstundkultur.name: Bundesministerium für Wohnen, Kunst, Kultur, Medien und Sport
bundesministeriumfrkunstundkultur.what: Austria's federal ministry for housing, arts, culture, media and sport, in Vienna, known until March 2025 as the Bundesministerium für Kunst, Kultur, öffentlichen Dienst und Sport.
bundesministeriumfrkunstundkultur.money: The federal budget of Austria: EUR 1.01 billion in 2022.
bundesministeriumfrkunstundkultur.arts: Its portfolio covers the arts, the federal theatres, film funding and museums.

burdockbrewery.name: Burdock Brewery
burdockbrewery.what: A craft brewery in downtown Toronto, brewing since 2015, with a restaurant and music hall on Bloor Street and a tavern in Kensington.
burdockbrewery.money: Sales of its beer online, wholesale and at its own restaurant, tavern and music hall.

busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.name: Busan Metropolitan City
busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.what: The city government of Busan, South Korea's second most populous city, led by Mayor Jeon Jae-soo.
busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.money: Local taxes (5.38 trillion won), national subsidies (7.79 trillion won) and allocation tax in its 19.35 trillion won budget proposed for 2027.

cafesjian.name: Cafesjian Family Foundation Inc.
cafesjian.what: A US family foundation in Shoreview, Minnesota, founded by Gerard L. Cafesjian, a former executive vice president of the legal publisher West Publishing, who died in 2013.
cafesjian.money: An endowment from its founder; assets were USD 55.4 million in 2023, when it paid USD 1.67 million in grants.
cafesjian.arts: Its founder also set up the Cafesjian Center for the Arts in Yerevan.

cairnsartgallery.name: Cairns Art Gallery Foundation
cairnsartgallery.what: The fundraising foundation of Cairns Art Gallery, set up in 2000, registered as a charity with the ACNC and run by a volunteer board of local professionals.
cairnsartgallery.money: Donations it raises, all spent on buying artworks for the gallery's permanent collection.
cairnsartgallery.arts: It has given more than AUD 840,000 toward the purchase of 79 works by 28 artists.

caissedepargnecepac.name: Caisse d'Epargne CEPAC
caissedepargnecepac.what: A cooperative savings bank in Groupe BPCE, formed in 1991 and based in Marseille, serving Provence, Corsica and French overseas territories in 13 départements.
caissedepargnecepac.money: Retail and business banking, notably housing, healthcare and energy transition loans, under a cooperative model with about 320,000 member shareholders.
caissedepargnecepac.arts: It spends nearly EUR 6 million a year on average on sponsorship, CSR and microloans, and supports the CEPAC Silo performance hall in Marseille.

californiaartscouncil|United States.name: California Arts Council
californiaartscouncil|United States.what: A California state agency in Sacramento, founded in 1976 under Governor Jerry Brown; the governor and the state legislature appoint its eight council members.
californiaartscouncil|United States.money: State budget funds, plus proceeds of the California Arts License Plate and voluntary contributions.
californiaartscouncil|United States.arts: On 14 August 2026 the council allocated nearly $24.6 million for 1,200 grants to nonprofit organisations and units of government.

californiainstituteofarts.name: California Institute of the Arts
californiainstituteofarts.what: A private art school in Santa Clarita, California, formed in 1961 by Walt and Roy Disney through the merger of Chouinard Art Institute and the Los Angeles Conservatory of Music.
californiainstituteofarts.money: Program services brought in $82,980,132 of its $122,015,803 revenue in 2024 to 2025, and contributions $10,472,635.
californiainstituteofarts.arts: With the Herb Alpert Foundation it set up the Alpert Award in the Arts in 1994, a yearly $75,000 fellowship for each of five artists.

caloustegulbenkian.name: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian
caloustegulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon on 18 July 1956 under the will of Calouste Sarkis Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it has a UK Branch and Paris centre.
caloustegulbenkian.money: The endowment Gulbenkian left from his oil fortune; it owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.
caloustegulbenkian.arts: It runs the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon, which holds Gulbenkian's art collection.

calq.name: Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec
calq.what: A public agency set up by the Government of Quebec in 1994 to fund professional artists, writers and arts organisations.
calq.money: The Government of Quebec; its 2024-2025 budget for grants and administration was C$191.8 million.
calq.arts: In 2024-2025 it granted more than C$178.6 million, including 2,011 individual grants and support for 900 organisations.
calq.address: 79 boulevard René-Lévesque Est, 3e étage, Québec, QC G1R 5N5

cambridgecitycouncil|UK.name: Cambridge City Council
cambridgecitycouncil|UK.what: The district council for the city of Cambridge in Cambridgeshire, England, which meets at Cambridge Guildhall; no party has held overall control since 2026.
cambridgecitycouncil|UK.money: The municipal budget of Cambridge City Council.

camper.name: Camper
camper.what: A Spanish shoe company founded in 1975 in Inca, Mallorca, by Lorenzo Fluxà, grandson of a Mallorcan cobbler, and led by the fourth generation of the Fluxà family.
camper.money: Sales of its shoes, around 4 million pairs a year, through more than 400 stores in 40 countries.

camposfamilyfirmsnutriasia.name: Nutri-Asia, Inc.
camposfamilyfirmsnutriasia.what: A Philippine food company founded on 1 October 1990 by Joselito D. Campos Jr., son of Unilab founder Jose Yao Campos; based at JY Campos Centre, Taguig.
camposfamilyfirmsnutriasia.money: Sales of sauces, seasonings and cooking oils under brands such as Datu Puti, Mang Tomas, UFC and Silver Swan; it holds Del Monte Pacific.
camposfamilyfirmsnutriasia.address: JY Campos Centre, 9th Avenue corner 30th Street, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig

canada.name: Government of Canada
canada.what: The federal executive of Canada, made up of the Cabinet under Prime Minister Mark Carney and over 103 departments and agencies.

canadacouncilforarts|Canada.name: Canada Council for the Arts
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.what: Canada's public arts funder, a federal Crown corporation set up in 1957 that reports to Parliament through the Minister of Canadian Heritage; based in Ottawa.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.money: Annual appropriations from the Parliament of Canada, plus income from its endowment, donations and bequests.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.arts: It also runs the Canada Council Art Bank, which rents out its collection of contemporary Canadian art.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.address: 150 Elgin St, 2nd floor, Ottawa, Ontario K2P 1L4

canadalife.name: The Canada Life Assurance Company
canadalife.what: A Canadian insurer founded in 1847 in Hamilton, combined in 2020 with Great-West Life and London Life, with its head office in Winnipeg.
canadalife.money: Its insurance and wealth business; it is wholly owned by Great-West Lifeco, about 72% owned by Power Financial Corporation.
canadalife.address: 100 Osborne Street North, Winnipeg, MB R3C 1V3

canadianheritage.name: Canadian Heritage
canadianheritage.what: The Government of Canada's department for arts, culture, broadcasting, official languages and sport, created in 1993 and headquartered in the Jules Léger Building, Gatineau, Quebec.
canadianheritage.money: The federal budget of the Government of Canada: CA$3.89 billion for the department in 2020.
canadianheritage.address: Jules Léger Building (South), Terrasses de la Chaudière, Gatineau, Quebec

canica.name: Canica AS
canica.what: The Hagen family's investment company in Oslo, set up in 1985 by Stein Erik Hagen, who died in 2026; Caroline Marie Hagen Kjos has controlled it since May 2026.
canica.money: Returns on its financial, industrial and real estate investments, including 196,351,000 shares in Orkla, of which it is the largest shareholder.
canica.arts: It owns a collection of mainly Nordic 19th and 20th century art, including Asger Jorn and Edvard Munch, and lends works to exhibitions.

canon.name: Canon Inc.
canon.what: A Japanese maker of cameras, printers, medical and semiconductor equipment, set up in 1937 as Precision Optical Instruments and headquartered in Shimomaruko, Ōta, Tokyo.
canon.money: Sales of optical, imaging, medical and industrial products worldwide; revenue was ¥4.03 trillion in 2022.

cantonofgeneva.name: République et canton de Genève
cantonofgeneva.what: One of the 26 cantons of Switzerland, a Swiss canton since 19 May 1815, governed by a Conseil d'État of seven members and a Grand Conseil of 100.
cantonofgeneva.arts: Its Service cantonal de la culture committed 47,805,598 francs in 2025, 14 percent more than in 2024; a culture promotion law has applied since January 2024.

cantonofneuchtel.name: République et Canton de Neuchâtel
cantonofneuchtel.what: A Swiss canton, a republic since the revolution of 1 March 1848, with a five-member Conseil d'État, a 100-seat Grand Conseil and 180,365 residents at the end of 2025.
cantonofneuchtel.money: The cantonal budget, with operating revenue of CHF 2,444,590,150 for 2026, adopted by the Grand Conseil on 2 December 2025.

cantonofsarajevo.name: Vlada Kantona Sarajevo
cantonofsarajevo.what: The government of Sarajevo Canton, a canton of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina established in 1995, led by a prime minister and a cabinet.

cantonofzurich.name: Kanton Zürich
cantonofzurich.what: A Swiss canton that joined the Swiss Confederacy in 1351, governed by a seven-member Regierungsrat and a 180-seat Cantonal Council.
cantonofzurich.money: The cantonal budget, in which the Cantonal Council raised the culture funding budget from 2026.
cantonofzurich.arts: Its Fachstelle Kultur, under the Direktion der Justiz und des Innern, pays operating grants to cultural institutions, as a rule for four years.

carlowcountycouncil|Ireland.name: Carlow County Council
carlowcountycouncil|Ireland.what: The local authority of County Carlow, Ireland, governed by the Local Government Act 2001, with 18 elected members and a chief executive, Coilín O'Reilly.
carlowcountycouncil|Ireland.money: Its draft 2026 budget set EUR 83.3 million of spending; the Department of Housing allocated it EUR 9.214 million of local property tax.

carlowleo.name: Local Enterprise Office Carlow
carlowleo.what: The County Carlow office in Ireland’s network of 31 Local Enterprise Offices, which advise small businesses and give them grants; it sits in Carlow town.
carlowleo.money: Irish state money through Enterprise Ireland, the agency of the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment that operates the 31 offices.
carlowleo.address: Enterprise House, O’Brien Road, Carlow, R93 YOY3

carolynclarkpowers.name: Carolyn Clark Powers
carolynclarkpowers.what: A Los Angeles philanthropist raised in Tulsa, Oklahoma, who joined the MOCA board in 2009, was its president for seven years and now chairs it.
carolynclarkpowers.arts: She co-chaired the Los Angeles Philharmonic's opening night gala from 2007 to 2012 and co-chairs the Dockery Farms Foundation in Mississippi.

carter.name: Amon G. Carter Foundation
carter.what: A Texas private foundation incorporated in 1945 by Amon G. Carter, publisher of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, and his wife Nenetta Burton Carter, based in Fort Worth.
carter.money: An endowment seeded in 1947 with $8,511,712 from the sale of the Carters' Wasson Field oil interests; net assets were $553,053,361 in 2024.
carter.arts: Its grants cover art and culture among other fields, and its charitable gifts passed $900 million by 31 December 2025.
carter.address: 201 Main Street, Suite 1945, Fort Worth, TX 76102

casinosaustria.name: Casinos Austria AG
casinosaustria.what: An Austrian casino company founded in 1967 and based in Vienna; the Czech group Allwyn is its main shareholder and the state holding ÖBAG holds 33.24%.
casinosaustria.money: Gambling: its casinos and Austrian lotteries business brought gross gaming revenue of €1.56 billion in 2025.

cassaruralealtogarda.name: Cassa Rurale AltoGarda - Rovereto
cassaruralealtogarda.what: A cooperative credit bank in Trentino, formed on 1 July 2021 from rural banks dating back to 1892, with over 15,600 members and offices in Arco and Rovereto.
cassaruralealtogarda.money: Its banking business with members and customers.

caterpillarannounced.name: Caterpillar Foundation
caterpillarannounced.what: The philanthropic arm of Caterpillar Inc., the construction and mining equipment maker based in Irving, Texas; it has given to more than 11,000 organisations in 110 countries since 1952.
caterpillarannounced.money: Gifts of USD 60.2 million in 2023, according to its IRS return, plus income on assets of USD 194 million.

cattolicaassicurazioni.name: Cattolica Assicurazioni
cattolicaassicurazioni.what: An Italian insurer founded as a cooperative in Verona in 1896, controlled by Generali since 2021 and a division and brand of Generali Italia since July 2023.
cattolicaassicurazioni.money: Insurance premiums, within the Generali group, which held 95.1 percent of the company by July 2022 and delisted it that August.

cavendishfarms.name: Cavendish Farms
cavendishfarms.what: A frozen potato processor owned by J.D. Irving, Limited, the New Brunswick group founded in 1882; it is North America's fourth largest processor of frozen potato products.
cavendishfarms.money: Sales of frozen fries, potato products and appetizers from its plants in Canada and the United States.

cbkrotterdam.name: Stichting Centrum Beeldende Kunst
cbkrotterdam.what: Rotterdam’s centre for visual art, a municipal service until 1 January 2006, when it became an independent foundation with a supervisory board; it runs SIR, BKOR, Art Office and TENT.
cbkrotterdam.money: Subsidies, mainly the City of Rotterdam’s culture plan grant: government subsidies were €4.02 million of its €4.47 million income in 2025.
cbkrotterdam.arts: It gave €969,760 in subsidies and grants in 2025.

ccpar.name: Companhia Carioca de Parcerias e Investimentos
ccpar.what: A Rio de Janeiro municipal company for concessions and public-private partnerships, created in June 2022 by Law 251/22, that took over Cdurp, which ran Porto Maravilha.
ccpar.money: The municipality of Rio de Janeiro, its owner.
ccpar.address: Rua Sacadura Cabral 133, Saúde, Rio de Janeiro

cemex.name: CEMEX, S.A.B. de C.V.
cemex.what: A Mexican building materials company that began in 1920 as Cementos Portland Monterrey, seated in San Pedro Garza García, Nuevo León.
cemex.money: Sales of cement, ready-mix concrete and aggregates: about USD 13 billion revenue in 2020.
cemex.arts: It gives the Premio CEMEX, an annual award for works in sustainability, accessibility, construction and architecture.

centurybank.name: Century Bank
centurybank.what: A locally owned, state-chartered community bank in Santa Fe, New Mexico, founded in 1887 as the Mutual Building and Loan Association.
centurybank.money: Lending, deposits and wealth management in New Mexico; total assets were USD 1.36 billion on 30 June 2026, according to the FDIC.
centurybank.address: 100 S Federal Pl, Santa Fe, NM

cesine.name: CESINE Centro Universitario
cesine.what: A private university centre for business, communication and design in Santander, set up in 1993 and part of the French school group EDH (Écoles Denis-Huisman).
cesine.money: Student fees for its official degrees and for top-up degrees certified by London Metropolitan University.

cfao.name: CFAO
cfao.what: A French distribution group in Africa for nearly 175 years, now a subsidiary of Japan's Toyota Tsusho Corporation, with headquarters in Boulogne-Billancourt.
cfao.money: Sales of vehicles, medicines, consumer goods and renewable power in 40 African countries; revenue EUR 9.1 billion, 91 percent of it in Africa.
cfao.arts: With Toyota Tsusho it runs the Toyota Tsusho CFAO African Art Award; works by the first edition's five laureates went on show in Japan in 2026.

chadwickloher.name: Chadwick-Loher Foundation
chadwickloher.what: A private foundation in Minneapolis, Minnesota, tax-exempt since 2003, with John W. Dayton as president and Chadwick L. Dayton as secretary.
chadwickloher.money: Returns on its investments, chiefly asset sales, on net assets of USD 3.85 million at the end of 2024; it gave USD 950,237 that year.

chairedbymiucciaprada.name: Prada S.p.A.
chairedbymiucciaprada.what: An Italian luxury fashion group founded in Milan in 1913 by Mario Prada, listed in Hong Kong, with Miuccia Prada as executive director and Patrizio Bertelli as chairman.
chairedbymiucciaprada.money: Sales of luxury goods under the Prada, Miu Miu, Church's and Versace brands, with net revenues of €5.7 billion in 2025.
chairedbymiucciaprada.arts: The group lists Fondazione Prada, the Milan contemporary art institution active since 1993, among its sponsorships.

chairmankoichinezu.name: Tobu Railway Co., Ltd.
chairmankoichinezu.what: A Tokyo private railway company founded on 1 November 1897, which Nezu Kaichirō led as president from 1905 and which belongs to the Fuyo Group.
chairmankoichinezu.money: Rail fares in the Kanto region, plus bus and taxi services, real estate, retail and the Tokyo Skytree.
chairmankoichinezu.arts: Nezu Kaichirō's collection of Japanese and East Asian art became the Nezu Museum, established on his death in 1940.
chairmankoichinezu.wrong_match: The museum sentence names Koichi Nezu and Yoshizumi Nezu as board links to the Tobu group and does not say Tobu Railway funds the museum.

chanelforworthexhibition.name: Chanel
chanelforworthexhibition.what: A luxury fashion house founded by Coco Chanel in Paris in 1910, privately owned by Alain and Gérard Wertheimer through Chanel Limited of London; its French arm sits in Neuilly-sur-Seine.
chanelforworthexhibition.money: Sales of fashion, fragrance and beauty products; revenue was USD 19.3 billion in 2025 and net profit USD 2.9 billion.

changwoncity|South Korea.name: Changwon City
changwoncity|South Korea.what: The city government of Changwon, capital of South Gyeongsang Province, South Korea, formed when Changwon, Masan and Jinhae merged on 1 July 2010.
changwoncity|South Korea.money: The municipal budget of Changwon, a city of about 1.0 million people.
changwoncity|South Korea.arts: It holds the Changwon Sculpture Biennale in honour of the sculptor Moon Shin.

chariloto.name: Chari-Loto Co., Ltd.
chariloto.what: A Tokyo company founded in 2006 that sells keirin and auto race betting tickets online and runs velodromes; a wholly owned subsidiary of MIXI since March 2019.
chariloto.money: Betting ticket sales on keirin cycle races and auto races through its Chari-Loto site, plus velodromes it owns or runs, including Toyama and Ito Onsen.
chariloto.address: Shibuya Scramble Square 36F, 2-24-12 Shibuya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo

charitiesaid.name: Charities Aid Foundation
charitiesaid.what: A registered charity that handles giving for donors and companies and owns CAF Bank; it began in 1924 inside the National Council of Social Service and became independent in 1974.
charitiesaid.money: Money that individuals, companies and foundations give through CAF for onward donation: £1.4 billion went to charities through it in 2025/26.
charitiesaid.address: 25 Kings Hill Avenue, Kings Hill, West Malling, Kent ME19 4TA

chase.name: Culture, Health, Arts, Sports and Education Fund
chase.what: A Jamaican company incorporated on 25 November 2002 under the Companies Act, based in Kingston, that funds culture, health, arts, sports and education.
chase.money: Monetary contributions from the lottery companies, which it receives, administers and distributes.
chase.arts: Its culture grants go to libraries, archives, historic sites, monuments, documentary film and cultural activities.

cherylsaban.name: The Saban Family Foundation
cherylsaban.what: A private grantmaking foundation in Los Angeles, tax exempt since January 2000, with Cheryl Saban as president and Haim Saban as senior vice president.
cherylsaban.money: Contributions received each year, $8,361,756 in 2024, and Haim Saban made his money in children's television and the 2001 sale of Fox Family Worldwide.

christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.name: The Christchurch Art Gallery Te Puna o Waiwhetū Foundation
christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.what: A charitable trust registered in 2008 as the CAG Artworks Trust to support Christchurch Art Gallery Te Puna o Waiwhetū, renamed in 2014 and again in 2024.
christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.money: Donations, partner gifts, gala dinners and auctions; its income was NZ$541,789 in the year to March 2026.
christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.arts: It funded Martin Creed's Work No. 2314 and helped buy Bill Hammond's Bone Yard Open Home for the gallery collection.
christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.address: Cnr Worcester Boulevard and Montreal Street, Christchurch 8140

christensveaas.name: Kistefos AS
christensveaas.what: A private investment company set up in 1998 and owned by the Norwegian investor Christen Sveaas, managed from Oslo.
christensveaas.money: Returns on its stakes in offshore, shipping, financial services, technology and real estate companies, mainly in Europe.

christensveaasart.name: Christen Sveaas' Kunststiftelse
christensveaasart.what: A Norwegian foundation set up in October 2019 by Christen Sveaas, owner of the investment company Kistefos AS, to manage, protect and lend his art collection.
christensveaasart.money: Gifts from Christen Sveaas: about 800 works from his private collection in 2020, with later donations taking the total past 850.

chubb.name: Chubb Limited
chubb.what: An insurer incorporated and headquartered in Zurich and listed on the New York Stock Exchange, founded as ACE Limited in Bermuda in 1985.
chubb.money: Premiums and investment income from property, casualty, accident, health, reinsurance and life insurance; revenue was US$59.4 billion in 2025.

chugokubank.name: The Chugoku Bank, Ltd.
chugokubank.what: A regional bank founded in Okayama on 21 December 1930, a subsidiary since October 2022 of the holding company Chugin Financial Group.
chugokubank.money: Banking; Chugin Financial Group reported total assets of ¥10.76 trillion and deposits of ¥8.31 trillion for 2024.

churchilldownsincorporated.name: Churchill Downs Incorporated
churchilldownsincorporated.what: A US racing, casino and online wagering company based in Louisville, Kentucky, which grew from the Churchill Downs racetrack, opened in 1875 as home of the Kentucky Derby.
churchilldownsincorporated.money: Its racetracks, casinos and the online wagering service TwinSpires: revenue of USD 2.93 billion in 2025.
churchilldownsincorporated.address: 600 N. Hurstbourne Parkway, Suite 400, Louisville, KY 40222

cincinnatimuseumassociation.name: Cincinnati Museum Association
cincinnatimuseumassociation.what: A nonprofit corporation incorporated in Cincinnati in 1881, after the work of the Women's Art Museum Association, to run the Cincinnati Art Museum in Eden Park.
cincinnatimuseumassociation.money: Contributions of $15.6 million and investment income of $8.8 million made up most of its $29.5 million revenue in the year to August 2025.

citibank.name: Citigroup Inc.
citibank.what: An American bank holding company in New York, formed in 1998 by merging Citicorp, parent of Citibank (chartered 1812), with Travelers.
citibank.money: Banking and financial services; it is the third-largest US banking institution by assets.

citifm.name: Citi 97.3 FM
citifm.what: A private radio station in Accra that began broadcasting on 5 November 2004, founded by Nik Amarteifio and led by managing director Samuel Attah-Mensah.
citifm.money: It is owned and run by Omni Media Ltd, which also operates the news site Citinewsroom.com.

cittmetropolitana.name: Città metropolitana di Firenze
cittmetropolitana.what: The metropolitan city of Florence, a local authority of 41 municipalities in Tuscany that replaced the Province of Florence on 1 January 2015 under Law 56/2014.
cittmetropolitana.money: The budget of the Città metropolitana di Firenze.

citybridge|UK.name: Bridge House Estates
citybridge|UK.what: The working name of Bridge House Estates, a London charity established by royal charter in 1282 to maintain London Bridge; its sole trustee is the City of London Corporation.
citybridge|UK.money: Income from its property and investment endowment: £31.2 million of £42.6 million income in the year to March 2025.

citygovernment|aros.name: Aarhus Kommune
citygovernment|aros.what: The municipality of Aarhus in the Central Denmark Region, run by a city council of 31 members under a magistrate system; Anders Winnerskjold is mayor.
citygovernment|aros.money: The municipal budget of Aarhus, set by the city council.

citygovernment|dundee-contemporary-arts.name: Dundee City Council
citygovernment|dundee-contemporary-arts.what: The local authority for Dundee City, one of the 32 council areas of Scotland, created in its modern form in 1996.
citygovernment|dundee-contemporary-arts.money: A revenue budget of £502 million for 2026 to 2027; council tax funds 18 percent of the budget.
citygovernment|dundee-contemporary-arts.address: Dundee House, 50 North Lindsay Street, Dundee DD1 1QE

citygovernment|kamloops-art-gallery.name: City of Kamloops
citygovernment|kamloops-art-gallery.what: The municipal government of Kamloops, British Columbia, a city incorporated in 1893 and amalgamated in 1973, run by an elected city council.
citygovernment|kamloops-art-gallery.money: Property taxes collected from homeowners each July, set through a yearly budget and five-year financial plan, with utilities on separate budgets.
citygovernment|kamloops-art-gallery.address: 7 Victoria Street West, Kamloops, BC V2C 1A2

citygovernment|kunsthalle-mannheim.name: Stadt Mannheim
citygovernment|kunsthalle-mannheim.what: The city government of Mannheim, an urban district of 319,536 inhabitants (31 December 2025) in Baden-Württemberg and the state's second most populous city.
citygovernment|kunsthalle-mannheim.money: The municipal budget, with ordinary revenue of 1,646,343,951 euros planned for 2026 after a second supplementary budget cut it by 82 million euros.
citygovernment|kunsthalle-mannheim.arts: The Kunsthalle Mannheim, founded for the city's 300th anniversary in 1907, is one of its municipal enterprises (Eigenbetriebe).

citygovernment|spike-island-bristol.name: Bristol City Council
citygovernment|spike-island-bristol.what: The local authority for Bristol, a unitary authority since 1996, based at City Hall on College Green; the Green Party has been its largest party since the 2024 election.
citygovernment|spike-island-bristol.money: Council tax, business rates, government grants and fees: council tax gives £316.54 million of the £634.1 million net revenue budget for 2026 to 2027.

cityofamsterdam|Netherlands.name: Gemeente Amsterdam
cityofamsterdam|Netherlands.what: The municipality of Amsterdam, the Dutch capital, governed by an elected city council and an executive of mayor and aldermen from the city hall at Amstel 1.
cityofamsterdam|Netherlands.money: Its municipal budget: income forecast at €7.75 billion for 2026, down from €8.1 billion, partly because the national government gives municipalities less.
cityofamsterdam|Netherlands.arts: Its 2026 budget set aside €28.5 million for the Amsterdam Museum's renovation and €3.2 million for H'ART Museum.

cityofatlanta|USA.name: Mayor's Office of Cultural Affairs, City of Atlanta
cityofatlanta|USA.what: An office of the Mayor of Atlanta, established in 1974 to support the city's cultural resources.
cityofatlanta|USA.money: The City of Atlanta's municipal budget.
cityofatlanta|USA.arts: It runs the Municipal Support for the Arts grants, the Public Art Program, the Atlanta Jazz Festival and the Chastain Arts Center.

cityofavignon|France.name: Ville d'Avignon
cityofavignon|France.what: The commune of Avignon, prefecture of the Vaucluse department in Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, with 92,188 residents in 2023.

cityofballarat|Australia.name: City of Ballarat
cityofballarat|Australia.what: The local council for Ballarat in western Victoria, formed on 6 May 1994 by merging the City of Ballaarat, the Shire of Ballarat and the Borough of Sebastopol.
cityofballarat|Australia.money: Property rates and charges, calculated from property valuations and limited by the Victorian Government's rate cap.
cityofballarat|Australia.arts: It has owned the Art Gallery of Ballarat since 1977 and pays its operating costs.
cityofballarat|Australia.address: The Phoenix, 25 Armstrong Street South, Ballarat VIC 3350

cityofbergamo|Italy.name: Comune di Bergamo
cityofbergamo|Italy.what: The municipal government of Bergamo, the fourth largest city in Lombardy, led by Mayor Elena Carnevali.
cityofbergamo|Italy.money: The Comune di Bergamo's municipal budget.
cityofbergamo|Italy.arts: With TenarisDalmine it is a founding member of GAMeC, the public-private gallery of modern and contemporary art that opened in 1991.

cityofbielefeld|Germany.name: Stadt Bielefeld
cityofbielefeld|Germany.what: The city of Bielefeld, a public-law corporation in North Rhine-Westphalia and the largest city of Ostwestfalen-Lippe, with 331,419 residents at the end of 2025.
cityofbielefeld|Germany.money: The municipal budget of the city of Bielefeld.

cityofbilbao|Spain.name: Ayuntamiento de Bilbao
cityofbilbao|Spain.what: The city council of Bilbao, made up of the mayor, a governing board and a municipal plenary, with its seat at Bilbao City Hall on Plaza Ernesto Erkoreka.
cityofbilbao|Spain.money: The municipal budget: 751 million euros for 2026, 32 million more than in 2025, approved without new debt.
cityofbilbao|Spain.arts: Its 2026 budget plan gives the culture directorate 49,817,713 euros; Teatro Arriaga receives 8.1 million euros and Bilbaoarte 1,068,356 euros.

cityofbrussels|Belgium.name: Ville de Bruxelles / Stad Brussel
cityofbrussels|Belgium.what: The municipal government of the City of Brussels, capital of Belgium and the largest municipality of the Brussels-Capital Region, with 196,828 inhabitants in January 2024.
cityofbrussels|Belgium.money: The city budget: more than EUR 1.1 billion of ordinary spending in 2025, with tax revenue of EUR 455.9 million as its largest source.

comunedimilano|Italy.what: The municipality of Milan, capital of Lombardy, whose administration has sat in Palazzo Marino since 1861.

comunidaddemadrid.name: Comunidad de Madrid
comunidaddemadrid.what: One of Spain's seventeen autonomous communities, created in 1983 around the capital, Madrid, with 7,113,886 inhabitants in 2025.
comunidaddemadrid.money: The regional budget of the Comunidad de Madrid.

conedison.name: Consolidated Edison, Inc.
conedison.what: A New York City energy company whose earliest predecessor, the New York Gas Light Company, was incorporated in 1823; its main subsidiary is the utility CECONY.
conedison.money: Regulated electric, gas and steam service in New York City and Westchester County; revenue was US$16.9 billion in 2025.

confindustriacomo.name: Confindustria Como
confindustriacomo.what: The association of industrial companies in the province of Como, active since 1919 and a member of Confindustria, the Italian industry confederation.

conocophillips.name: ConocoPhillips
conocophillips.what: A US oil and gas exploration and production company in Houston, formed in 2002 when Conoco Inc. and Phillips Petroleum merged.
conocophillips.money: Sales of crude oil, bitumen, natural gas and LNG: USD 56.95 billion revenue in 2024; it holds 3.125 percent of Qatar's North Field East venture.

conseildesartsdemontral.name: Conseil des arts de Montréal
conseildesartsdemontral.what: The arts council of the Urban Agglomeration of Montréal, active since 1956, which gives grants to Montréal artists, collectives and arts organisations.
conseildesartsdemontral.money: A yearly contribution from the agglomeration's budget: C$21,936,700 in 2025, frozen at the 2024 amount.
conseildesartsdemontral.arts: It invested C$19,528,703 in support programmes in 2025 and supported 763 organisations and collectives.
conseildesartsdemontral.address: 1210 Sherbrooke Street East, Montréal, QC H2L 1L9

consejonacionaldelpatrimoniocultural.name: Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural
consejonacionaldelpatrimoniocultural.what: The Cuban Ministry of Culture body, founded in 1995 and seated in Havana, that defines and declares the goods forming the nation's cultural heritage under Law No. 1.
consejonacionaldelpatrimoniocultural.money: The Cuban state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.
consejonacionaldelpatrimoniocultural.address: Calle 13 No. 810 esquina 4, Vedado, Plaza de la Revolución, Havana

conselldemallorca.name: Consell de Mallorca
conselldemallorca.what: The island government of Mallorca, created under Royal Decree-Law 18/1978 and first constituted on 24 April 1979, seated in the Palau del Consell in Palma.
conselldemallorca.money: Public funds set in its annual budget: EUR 761.7 million for 2026, approved in December 2025.

constructoracapital.name: Constructora Capital
constructoracapital.what: A Colombian housing developer from Antioquia, led by the brothers Felipe and Pablo Echeverri, that has built homes in Bogotá and Medellín for more than 34 years.
constructoracapital.money: Housing sales: COP 2.07 trillion in 2025 through Constructora Capital Bogotá SAS and Constructora Capital Medellín SAS.

continentalbarum.name: Continental Barum s.r.o.
continentalbarum.what: A tyre maker in Otrokovice, Czechia, registered in February 1993 as the joint venture of Barum and the German Continental group.
continentalbarum.money: Tyre sales from its Otrokovice plant, with capacity of up to 19 million car tyres a year; revenue was CZK 72.6 billion in 2025.

corefundersstichtingdoen.name: Stichting DOEN
corefundersstichtingdoen.what: A Dutch foundation in Amsterdam established in 1991 by the Postcode Loterij, the Dutch postcode lottery.
corefundersstichtingdoen.money: Annual contributions from two Dutch charity lotteries, the Postcode Loterij and the VriendenLoterij.
corefundersstichtingdoen.arts: It backs more than 250 initiatives with grants, loans and investment capital, and its VriendenLoterij Fonds covers arts and culture.

corningincorporatedismainfunder.name: Corning Incorporated
corningincorporatedismainfunder.what: An American technology company specialising in glass, ceramics and related materials, founded in 1851 by Amory Houghton as Bay State Glass Co. and headquartered in Corning, New York.
corningincorporatedismainfunder.money: Sales of specialty glass, ceramics, optical fibre and LCD glass, with revenue of US$15.63 billion in 2025.

cosmooil.name: Cosmo Oil Company, Limited
cosmooil.what: A Japanese oil refiner formed on 1 April 1986 by merging Maruzen Petroleum and Daikyo Petroleum, now a subsidiary of Cosmo Energy Holdings, based in Tokyo.
cosmooil.money: Refining and selling petroleum products from three refineries in Japan; revenue was JPY 3,537 billion in fiscal 2013.

cosmoscownameditmuseumofyear.name: Cosmoscow Foundation for Contemporary Art
cosmoscownameditmuseumofyear.what: The non-profit arm of Cosmoscow, the Moscow contemporary art fair started in 2010 by the collector Margarita Pushkina; the foundation was launched in 2017.
cosmoscownameditmuseumofyear.money: The Cosmoscow fair and its partners; Credit Suisse became a strategic partner of the fair in 2015.
cosmoscownameditmuseumofyear.arts: Each year it names a Museum of the Year and gives works to its collection, such as five works by Taus Makhacheva to the Pushkin Museum in 2018.

costopoulos.name: The J. F. Costopoulos Foundation
costopoulos.what: A private foundation set up in 1979, at the centenary of Credit Bank (now Alpha Bank), by its chairman Spyros Costopoulos and his wife Eurydice.
costopoulos.money: A donation from Spyros and Eurydice Costopoulos at its founding; its accounts are audited yearly and submitted to Greece's Ministry of Finance.
costopoulos.arts: It supports visual arts, theatre, music, cinema and dance, cultural heritage and research, and keeps a library and an art collection.

cottonon.name: Cotton On Foundation
cottonon.what: The charity of the Australian retailer Cotton On Group, started in Geelong in 2007 after a donation request for a healthcare centre in Mannya, Uganda.
cottonon.money: Proceeds from Foundation products sold in Cotton On Group stores and online, all of which go to its projects.

cova.name: Fondation d'entreprise Covéa
cova.what: The corporate foundation of Covéa, the French mutual insurance group behind MAAF, MMA and GMF; it was set up at the end of 2022 and launched in May 2023.
cova.money: Covéa's insurance business funds it, with a budget of about €4 million a year for social and human inclusion.

cragg.name: Cragg Foundation
cragg.what: A non-profit foundation set up in Wuppertal in 2005 by the family of the Anglo-German sculptor Tony Cragg; it runs the Waldfrieden Sculpture Park, opened in 2008.
cragg.money: The Cragg family, who set it up; Tony Cragg owns the Waldfrieden estate that it runs.

crankstart.name: Crankstart Foundation
crankstart.what: A US private foundation of Sir Michael Moritz and his wife Harriet Heyman, its chief executive and chief financial officer, tax exempt since June 2002.
crankstart.money: Contributions of USD 247.5 million in 2024, when its total assets were USD 4.39 billion.
crankstart.arts: It became the main sponsor of the Booker Prize in June 2019, for an initial five years.

crditagricole.name: Crédit Agricole Group
crditagricole.what: A French cooperative banking group, founded in 1894, of local banks, 39 regional banks and the listed central body Crédit Agricole S.A., headquartered in Montrouge.
crditagricole.money: Retail banking, insurance, asset management through Amundi and corporate banking: revenue of €39.56 billion and net income of €8.75 billion in 2025.

crditdunord.name: Crédit du Nord
crditdunord.what: A French retail bank seated in Lille, bought by Société Générale from Paribas in 1997 and merged with the Société Générale branch network into SG on 1 January 2023.
crditdunord.money: Banking income from retail and business customers of its regional banks; since 2023 that business belongs to SG, the French retail bank of Société Générale.

crditmutuelnordeurope.name: Crédit Mutuel Nord Europe
crditmutuelnordeurope.what: A mutual bank of the Crédit Mutuel group with its seat in Lille, 129 local caisses and 239 branches; part of Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale since 1 January 2022.
crditmutuelnordeurope.money: Banking and insurance for 982,066 clients, 657,073 of them member-owners (sociétaires), at the end of 2024; it also owns Beobank in Belgium.
crditmutuelnordeurope.arts: Its Fondation Crédit Mutuel Nord Europe, set up in 2013, funds culture, training, solidarity and environment projects and has paid out more than EUR 13 million.

creatensw.name: Create NSW
creatensw.what: The NSW Government's arts and culture agency, formed on 1 April 2017 from Arts NSW and Screen NSW.
creatensw.money: The New South Wales state budget, through the Minister for the Arts, who answers to the NSW Parliament.
creatensw.arts: Its Arts and Cultural Funding Program includes Creative Steps grants of up to $75,000 for new work by NSW artists.

creativeaustralia.name: Creative Australia
creativeaustralia.what: The Australian Government's principal arts investment and advisory body, founded as the Australia Council for the Arts in 1968 and renamed in 2023; based in Sydney.
creativeaustralia.money: The Australian Government, with funding decisions made at arm's length from the federal arts minister.

creativeeurope|Netherlands.name: Creative Europe
creativeeurope|Netherlands.what: The European Commission's programme for the cultural, creative and audiovisual sectors, run by its Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture with grants handled by EACEA.
creativeeurope|Netherlands.money: The European Union budget: EUR 2.44 billion for 2021-2027, up from EUR 1.47 billion in 2014-2020.

creativeindustriesnl.name: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie
creativeindustriesnl.what: The Dutch national culture fund for design, architecture and digital culture, a private-law foundation and independent administrative body active since 1 January 2013, based in Rotterdam.
creativeindustriesnl.money: State money from the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science, the parent ministry of the national culture funds (rijkscultuurfondsen).

creativenewzealand.name: Arts Council of New Zealand Toi Aotearoa
creativenewzealand.what: The national arts development agency of the New Zealand government, a Crown entity governed by the Arts Council, set up in 1994 to replace the Queen Elizabeth II Arts Council.
creativenewzealand.money: The New Zealand Lottery Grants Board Te Puna Tahua and the government through Vote: Arts, Culture and Heritage.
creativenewzealand.arts: It invested NZ$61 million in the arts in 2024/25.

creativescotland.name: Creative Scotland
creativescotland.what: The Scottish Government's public body for the arts, screen and creative industries, created in 2010 from the Scottish Arts Council and Scottish Screen; based in Edinburgh.
creativescotland.money: Funding from the Scottish Government and the National Lottery.
creativescotland.address: Waverley Court, 4 East Market Street, Edinburgh EH8 8BG

creativescotlandregularfunding.name: Creative Scotland
creativescotlandregularfunding.what: An executive non-departmental public body of the Scottish Government for the arts, screen and creative industries, created in 2010 from Scottish Screen and the Scottish Arts Council.
creativescotlandregularfunding.money: Funding from the Scottish Government and from the UK National Lottery, which it distributes to artists and cultural organisations in Scotland.
creativescotlandregularfunding.arts: Its Multi-Year Funding programme, which replaced Regular Funding, covers the core costs of cultural organisations from April 2025 to March 2028.
creativescotlandregularfunding.address: Waverley Court, 4 East Market Street, Edinburgh EH8 8BG

creativevictoria.name: Creative Victoria
creativevictoria.what: The Victorian state government's agency for the arts and creative industries, reporting to the Minister for Creative Industries; based in Melbourne.
creativevictoria.money: The budget of the State of Victoria.

croatiasministryofculture|Croatia.name: Ministarstvo kulture i medija Republike Hrvatske
croatiasministryofculture|Croatia.short: Croatian Ministry of Culture and Media
croatiasministryofculture|Croatia.what: The Croatian government ministry for culture and media, in its present form since 1994, led by Minister Nina Obuljen Koržinek since 19 October 2016.
croatiasministryofculture|Croatia.money: The Croatian state budget: the ministry's budget was €642 million for 2025.

ctdecd.name: Connecticut Department of Economic and Community Development
ctdecd.what: The State of Connecticut's economic development department; the Connecticut Office of the Arts, the state arts agency, sits within it.
ctdecd.money: Connecticut's state budget, plus National Endowment for the Arts funds that the Office of the Arts regrants.
ctdecd.arts: Its Office of the Arts made 232 Supporting Arts grants totalling US$1,050,005 in fiscal 2024.

cubanministryofculture|Cuba.name: Ministerio de Cultura de Cuba
cubanministryofculture|Cuba.what: The Cuban government ministry in charge of cultural policy, founded in 1976 under the Council of Ministers; its minister is Alpidio Alonso Grau.
cubanministryofculture|Cuba.address: Calle 2 No. 258, between 11 and 13, Plaza de la Revolución, La Habana

cullen.name: The Cullen Foundation
cullen.what: A private foundation in Houston set up in 1947 by the oilman Hugh Roy Cullen and his wife Lillie Cranz Cullen; family members still sit on its board.
cullen.money: First oil and gas working interests from the Cullens, sold off by 2000; since then a portfolio of marketable securities and other investments.
cullen.arts: It has given over $600 million since 1947 to arts, education, health care and public service, mostly in the Houston area.

culturalendowmentofestonia.name: Eesti Kultuurkapital
culturalendowmentofestonia.what: An Estonian legal person in public law, set up in 1925 and re-established in 1994, that funds the arts, folk culture, sport and cultural buildings.
culturalendowmentofestonia.money: Fixed shares of state taxes: 3.5 percent of alcohol and tobacco excise duty and 47.8 percent of gambling tax.

cultureireland.name: Culture Ireland
cultureireland.what: The Irish state agency that promotes Irish arts abroad, set up in 2005 in Dublin.
cultureireland.money: The Irish state budget through the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport: its budget was €6.6 million in 2023.
cultureireland.arts: Its January 2025 grant round gave over €1.5 million to 192 projects in over 34 countries.

cultureliverpool.name: Culture Liverpool
cultureliverpool.what: The culture and events service of Liverpool City Council, which stages major cultural and sporting events in the city.
cultureliverpool.money: Liverpool City Council's £817.6m net budget for 2026/27, made up of business rates £295.1m, council tax £277.0m and government grants £245.5m.
cultureliverpool.arts: The council's Culture and Arts Investment Programme funds 29 arts organisations; in September 2025 its cabinet proposed extending it to March 2027 with £2.245m.

cultureministry|Denmark.name: Kulturministeriet
cultureministry|Denmark.what: Denmark's ministry for culture, sport and media, founded in 1961 with Julius Bomholt as its first minister, based on Nybrogade in Copenhagen.
cultureministry|Denmark.money: The Danish state budget: section 21 of the Finance Act for 2026 sets the ministry's net spending at DKK 14,015.8 million.
cultureministry|Denmark.arts: Its agencies include the Danish Arts Foundation (Statens Kunstfond) and the Agency for Culture and Palaces.

culturenorway.name: Kulturdirektoratet
culturenorway.what: A Norwegian state directorate set up on 1 January 2023 as secretariat for Kulturrådet (Arts Council Norway), Statens kunstnerstipend and Fond for lyd og bilde.
culturenorway.money: The Norwegian state budget, through the Ministry of Culture and Equality.
culturenorway.arts: Kulturrådet, an independent body created in 1965, manages the Norwegian Cultural Fund; the directorate handles around 20,000 applications a year.

cultuurfonds.name: Cultuurfonds
cultuurfonds.what: A Dutch private foundation set up by Prince Bernhard in London in 1940, renamed in 2023 to drop his name, with its office in Amsterdam.
cultuurfonds.money: Proceeds from the VriendenLoterij and the Nederlandse Loterij, plus gifts and bequests from donors.
cultuurfonds.arts: It puts more than EUR 50 million a year into culture and nature.

cultuurfondsnoordholland.name: het Cultuurfonds Noord-Holland
cultuurfondsnoordholland.what: The Noord-Holland branch of the Cultuurfonds, the Dutch cultural fund Prince Bernhard set up in London in 1940; each province has a branch with its own board.
cultuurfondsnoordholland.money: The national Cultuurfonds, funded by the VriendenLoterij and Nederlandse Loterij, donors and bequests; the branch also manages named funds set up by private donors.
cultuurfondsnoordholland.arts: The Cultuurfonds gives more than 50 million euros a year to culture and nature; the branch judges applications for projects of regional importance.

cuyahogaarts.name: Cuyahoga Arts & Culture
cuyahogaarts.what: The public arts and culture funder of Cuyahoga County, Ohio, set up after county voters approved a dedicated arts tax in 2006.
cuyahogaarts.money: A county tax on cigarette sales, renewed by voters in 2015 and expanded in 2024; the levy runs to 2035.
cuyahogaarts.arts: Since 2007 it has made 4,600 grants worth $270 million to 500 nonprofit organizations.

czechtelevision.name: Česká televize
czechtelevision.what: The public television broadcaster of the Czech Republic, established in 1992 as successor to Czechoslovak Television, with headquarters at Kavčí hory in Prague.
czechtelevision.money: Television fees, which made up more than 90% of its income in the 2020 budget estimate, plus advertising.

daewoo.name: Daewoo Foundation
daewoo.what: A Seoul foundation for public welfare that began with medical aid on remote islands and was reborn as an independent foundation in the 2000s.
daewoo.money: A fund given from 1978 by Kim Woo-choong (1936 to 2019), founder and chairman of the Daewoo Group until its collapse in 1999.
daewoo.arts: Culture and the arts are one of its programme fields, beside health care, social welfare, scholarship and education.

dalhousie.name: Dalhousie University
dalhousie.what: A public research university in Halifax, Nova Scotia, established in 1818 as Dalhousie College by George Ramsay, 9th Earl of Dalhousie, then Lieutenant Governor of Nova Scotia.
dalhousie.money: Provincial operating grants and tuition fees, with an endowment of C$1.0074 billion in 2025.

danireissctoexpansion.name: Dani Reiss
danireissctoexpansion.what: Toronto businessman, chairman and chief executive of the parka maker Canada Goose; he took over as chief executive from his father, David Reiss, in 2001.
danireissctoexpansion.money: His wealth from Canada Goose, listed in Toronto and New York since 2017 and part owned by Bain Capital; revenue CA$1.35 billion in fiscal 2025.
danireissctoexpansion.renamed: The AGO gift came from Dani Reiss personally, not from the company Canada Goose.

danisharts.name: Statens Kunstfond
danisharts.what: Denmark's state arts fund, set up by law on 27 May 1964 and merged with the Danish Arts Council in 2014, with 16 expert committees that award its grants.
danisharts.money: The Danish state budget, through funds provided by the Ministry of Culture.
danisharts.arts: It awards about 640 million Danish kroner a year to some 6,000 projects through about 65 grant schemes.

danone.name: Danone
danone.what: A French food and beverage group, listed on Euronext Paris and based in Paris, whose Danone brand Isaac Carasso founded in Barcelona in 1919.
danone.money: Sales of dairy and plant-based products, bottled waters and specialised nutrition: 27.3 billion euros in 2025.

dardaniainsurancecompany.name: Dardania Insurance Company J.S.C.
dardaniainsurancecompany.what: A Kosovo insurance company based in Pristina, bought in 2014 by the insurer Eurosig.
dardaniainsurancecompany.money: Insurance premiums, including an EULEX Kosovo vehicle insurance contract worth up to EUR 800,000 a year, won with Eurosig in January 2015.

darlingtonbuildingsociety.name: Darlington Building Society
darlingtonbuildingsociety.what: A mutual building society owned by its members, formed in 1856 as the Darlington Working Men's Equitable Permanent Building Society, with its head office in Darlington.
darlingtonbuildingsociety.money: Mortgage lending funded by members' savings: retail deposits of 939 million pounds and total assets of 1,025 million pounds in 2025.
darlingtonbuildingsociety.arts: It gives 5 percent of its profits each year to local good causes.
darlingtonbuildingsociety.address: Sentinel House, Morton Road, Darlington DL1 4PT

darpa.name: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
darpa.what: The research agency of the US Department of Defense, founded in February 1958 as ARPA after the Soviet launch of Sputnik 1, in Arlington, Virginia.
darpa.money: The US defence budget: USD 4.322 billion in fiscal 2026.

davidgeffen.name: David Geffen
davidgeffen.what: American record and film executive, born in 1943, who co-founded Asylum Records in 1971, founded Geffen Records in 1980 and co-founded DreamWorks SKG in 1994.
davidgeffen.money: The 1990 sale of Geffen Records to MCA for shares then worth $550 million; Forbes estimated his net worth at $9 billion in 2024.
davidgeffen.arts: In 2021 he gave $150 million to the Yale School of Drama, which made tuition free and took his name.

davidzwirner.name: David Zwirner
davidzwirner.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded in New York in 1993 by the German-born dealer David Zwirner, with galleries in New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris and Hong Kong.
davidzwirner.money: Sales of works by the more than seventy artists and estates it represents, in the primary and secondary art markets.

davivienda.name: Banco Davivienda S.A.
davivienda.what: A Colombian private bank founded in Bogotá on 1 September 1972, part of Grupo Bolívar and the second largest bank in the country.
davivienda.money: Financial services for individuals and companies, with assets of COP 224.5 trillion in 2025.

dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.name: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.what: The UK government ministerial department for culture, media, sport and digital services, named the Department for Culture, Media and Sport from 2023 until its renaming in 2026.
dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.money: UK central government money, as a ministerial department of the UK government.
dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.arts: Its public bodies include Arts Council England, the British Museum, the National Gallery, Tate and the Victoria and Albert Museum.

debethune.name: De Bethune
debethune.what: An independent Swiss watch manufacturer founded in 2002 by Denis Flageollet and David Zanetta, with its workshops in L'Auberson near Sainte-Croix, in the canton of Vaud.
debethune.money: Sales of a few hundred mechanical watches a year; since Zanetta sold his majority share in 2017 it has four shareholders.

deborahloebbrice.name: Deborah L Brice Foundation
deborahloebbrice.what: A private foundation in New York, tax-exempt since 1971, with Deborah Loeb Brice, a granddaughter of Arthur Lehman and sister of Ambassador John L. Loeb Jr., as trustee.
deborahloebbrice.money: Investment income on its endowment: 1,026,742 dollars in dividends in 2024, with net assets of 25,486,275 dollars at the end of that year.

defrance.name: Fondation de France
defrance.what: A private foundation recognised as being of public utility, created by decree in 1969 at the wish of Charles de Gaulle and André Malraux; it sits in Paris.
defrance.money: Private donations collected from the public and from companies, plus the funds of the 974 foundations it shelters.
defrance.arts: It supported 13,000 projects in 2025; culture is one of its fields.

degroofpetercam.name: Degroof Petercam
degroofpetercam.what: A Brussels private bank founded as Banque Philippson in 1871, merged with the broker Petercam in 2015 and owned since 2024 by Crédit Agricole's Indosuez Wealth Management.
degroofpetercam.money: Fees and income from private banking, asset management, investment banking and asset services for private and institutional clients.

delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.name: De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde, Inc.
delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.what: A private Catholic non-stock, non-profit college in Malate, Manila, founded in 1988 by the De La Salle Brothers and a member of De La Salle Philippines.
delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.money: Tuition from its students; in 2019 the Supreme Court ruled its 2002 gross receipts of 643 million pesos exempt from tax.
delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.arts: It was the first school in the Philippines to offer degrees in animation, photography, film, multimedia arts and production design.

delenprivatebank.name: Delen Private Bank
delenprivatebank.what: An Antwerp private bank grown from the brokerage Delen & C°, founded by André Delen in 1936; Ackermans & van Haaren owns 78.75 percent, the Delen family 21.25 percent.
delenprivatebank.money: Fees for managing and planning the wealth of private clients and their companies.

delmontephilippines.name: Del Monte Philippines, Inc.
delmontephilippines.what: A Philippine food company 87 percent owned by Del Monte Pacific Limited, which is 72 percent owned by the Campos family's NutriAsia Pacific Group.
delmontephilippines.money: Sales of packaged fruit, juices, sauces and fresh pineapples grown on its 30,000-hectare leased plantation in Bukidnon and Misamis Oriental.
delmontephilippines.address: JY Campos Centre, 9th Avenue corner 30th Street, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig City 1634

deloitte.name: Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited
deloitte.what: A network of audit, consulting, tax and advisory firms that William Welch Deloitte founded in London in 1845; its coordinating company was incorporated in England in 2010.
deloitte.money: Fees its member firms earn from audit, consulting, tax and advisory work: aggregate revenue of US$67.2 billion in fiscal 2024.

denederlandschebank.name: De Nederlandsche Bank N.V.
denederlandschebank.what: The central bank of the Netherlands, founded by King William I in 1814, now a state-owned public limited company within the Eurosystem and the Dutch financial supervisor.
denederlandschebank.money: Income on its monetary assets; in 2025 interest costs exceeded it, for a loss of 967 million euros, so the Dutch state receives no dividend.

dentons.name: Dentons
dentons.what: A multinational law firm formed in March 2013 by merging SNR Denton, Fraser Milner Casgrain and Salans; a Swiss verein whose largest offices are in London and New York.
dentons.money: Legal fees: revenue of USD 2.899 billion in 2019.

denza.name: Shenzhen Denza New Energy Automotive Co., Ltd.
denza.what: A Chinese electric car brand founded in February 2011 as a 50-50 joint venture of BYD and Daimler; BYD became its sole shareholder in September 2024.
denza.money: Car sales; it is wholly owned by BYD, the Shenzhen electric vehicle maker.

deolifant.name: De Olifant BV
deolifant.what: A family-run wholesaler of paints, facade insulation and industrial coatings in the Antwerp area, in business for more than 30 years, with branches in Wommelgem and Wilrijk.
deolifant.money: Wholesale of professional paint and coating brands such as Caparol and Sigma.

departmentofculturecommunicationsandspor.name: Department of Culture, Communications and Sport
departmentofculturecommunicationsandspor.what: The Irish government department for arts, culture, media, communications and sport, led by the Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport, at Leeson Lane, Dublin.
departmentofculturecommunicationsandspor.money: The Irish state budget: Budget 2027 gives it €1.298 billion, of which €848 million is current spending.
departmentofculturecommunicationsandspor.arts: Budget 2027 gives the Arts Council over €143.5 million and funds the Basic Income for the Arts scheme in full.

deroytestamentary.name: DeRoy Testamentary Foundation
deroytestamentary.what: A private foundation in Michigan created under the will of Helen L. DeRoy (1882 to 1977), who ran her husband's car business, and tax-exempt since 1978.
deroytestamentary.money: Helen DeRoy's estate, built on Aaron DeRoy's Studebaker dealerships; in 2025 it spent 25.3 million dollars, leaving net assets of 272,970 dollars.

desjardins.name: Desjardins Group
desjardins.what: A Canadian financial services cooperative and the largest federation of credit unions in North America, founded on 6 December 1900 in Lévis, Quebec, by Alphonse Desjardins.
desjardins.money: Its cooperative banking business: surplus earnings of C$3,811 million in 2025, on assets of C$510.2 billion.

destandaard.name: De Standaard
destandaard.what: A Flemish daily newspaper published since 4 December 1918, with its newsroom on Kantersteen in central Brussels since late 2020.
destandaard.money: Its owner Mediahuis, a Belgian media company with revenue of EUR 1,236 million in 2024.
destandaard.wrong_match: M HKA lists De Standaard as a media partner, not as a funder.

detobelskefamiliefond.name: Det Obelske Familiefond
detobelskefamiliefond.what: A Danish family foundation set up in 1956 by Asta Obel of the Aalborg tobacco firm C.W. Obel; a descendant of hers chairs its board.
detobelskefamiliefond.money: Investments and property, held through C.W. Obel Holding and C.W. Obel Ejendomme, the other two units of the Obel group.
detobelskefamiliefond.arts: It gives DKK 135 million to 150 million a year to charity across contemporary art and classical music, social work and North Jutland.

deutschebrsephotography.name: Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation gGmbH
deutschebrsephotography.what: A non-profit corporate foundation of Deutsche Börse, the Frankfurt stock exchange group, set up in Frankfurt am Main in 2015.
deutschebrsephotography.money: Deutsche Börse, which began collecting contemporary photography in 1999 and in 2015 handed the foundation its collection and cultural sponsorship.
deutschebrsephotography.arts: It holds the Art Collection Deutsche Börse of more than 2,400 works by about 170 artists and awards an annual photography prize with the Photographers' Gallery, London.

deutschedenkmalschutz.name: Deutsche Stiftung Denkmalschutz
deutschedenkmalschutz.what: A privately funded foundation set up on 17 April 1985, the largest private initiative for monument preservation in Germany, with its seat in Bonn.
deutschedenkmalschutz.money: Gifts from about 200,000 private donors and money from the GlücksSpirale lottery.
deutschedenkmalschutz.arts: It has helped preserve more than 7,400 monuments with almost 800 million euros in funding.

deutscheklassenlotterie.name: Stiftung Deutsche Klassenlotterie Berlin
deutscheklassenlotterie.what: A public-law foundation set up by the State of Berlin under a law of 7 June 1974, operating since 1 January 1975 and supervised by the Senate's interior department.
deutscheklassenlotterie.money: A levy of 20 percent of stakes plus the balance-sheet profit of Deutsche Klassenlotterie Berlin, the Berlin lottery, fixed by law.
deutscheklassenlotterie.arts: It funds social, environmental, civic and cultural projects in Berlin and reports on its grants to the Berlin parliament every quarter.

diaartendowment.name: Dia Art Foundation
diaartendowment.what: A New York nonprofit for contemporary art, set up in 1974 by Philippa de Menil, the art dealer Heiner Friedrich and the art historian Helen Winkler.
diaartendowment.money: Founded on Philippa de Menil's Schlumberger oil fortune; today contributions and investment income, $24,122,046 and $14,446,583 in the year to June 2025.
diaartendowment.arts: It maintains long-term installations and site-specific projects beyond its exhibition spaces at Dia Beacon and Dia Chelsea.

didrichsenart.name: Didrichsens konstmuseum sr
didrichsenart.what: A foundation set up on 11 November 1963 by Marie-Louise and Gunnar Didrichsen to preserve their art collections and museum building on Kuusisaari island in Helsinki.
didrichsenart.money: The founders' fortune; Gunnar Didrichsen, a Danish businessman, founded the import company Transmeri in Finland in 1927.

digitalrealty.name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
digitalrealty.what: A US real estate investment trust that owns and operates data centres worldwide, formed in 2004 by GI Partners and headquartered in Austin, Texas.
digitalrealty.money: Rent and fees for data centre space, colocation and interconnection: revenue of 6.11 billion dollars in 2025.

dior.name: Christian Dior Couture
dior.what: A Paris fashion house founded in 1946 by the designer Christian Dior with the textile industrialist Marcel Boussac, now a subsidiary of LVMH.
dior.money: Sales of its fashion and leather goods; its parent group is controlled by Bernard Arnault's family, which holds 97.5% of Christian Dior SE.

directorategeneralforarts.name: Direção-Geral das Artes
directorategeneralforarts.what: The Portuguese government's directorate-general for the arts, which coordinates state support policies for the arts from its offices at Campo Grande in Lisbon.
directorategeneralforarts.money: Portuguese State funds for arts support, which it sets out each year in its Declaração Anual.
directorategeneralforarts.arts: Its Programa de Apoio a Projetos 2025 had €13.35 million for six competitions, the same amount as in 2023 and 2024.

distritodebogot.name: Bogotá, Distrito Capital
distritodebogot.what: The capital district of Colombia, a first-order territorial entity formed in 1954 and governed by the Alcaldía Mayor, which sits in the Palacio Liévano on the Plaza de Bolívar.
distritodebogot.money: The budget of the Bogotá capital district.

dlgsc.name: Department of Creative Industries, Tourism and Sport
dlgsc.what: A Western Australian government department formed on 1 July 2025, when it took over the creative industries and sport work of the Department of Local Government, Sport and Cultural Industries.
dlgsc.arts: Its arts funding includes Arts Projects for Organisations, the Contemporary Music Fund and the Regional Aboriginal Arts Development programme.

dmgmori.name: DMG MORI AKTIENGESELLSCHAFT
dmgmori.what: A Bielefeld maker of CNC lathes, milling machines and other machine tools, formerly Gildemeister AG, controlled since 2016 by a holding company of the Japanese DMG MORI group.
dmgmori.money: Sales of machine tools, automation and services to manufacturers: 2,228.3 million euros in 2024, 59 percent of it outside Germany.

dnv.name: DNV
dnv.what: A Norwegian classification society and assurance company for shipping, energy and other industries, headquartered in Høvik and owned by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation.
dnv.money: Fees for ship classification, certification, testing and advisory work: operating revenue of 34,966 million Norwegian kroner in 2024.

do.name: DO & CO Aktiengesellschaft
do.what: A Vienna catering group founded by Attila Dogudan and listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange since 1998, serving airlines, rail operators and international events.
do.money: Catering revenue of about 2.46 billion euros in the 2025/26 financial year, of which airline catering brought 1.95 billion euros.

doen.name: Stichting DOEN
doen.what: A Dutch foundation set up in 1991 by the Postcode Loterij that funds pioneers in the Netherlands and abroad.
doen.money: Lottery proceeds: 24,303,520 euros from the Postcode Loterij and 7,200,000 euros from the VriendenLoterij in 2025.
doen.arts: Its VriendenLoterij Fonds funded 70 art and culture projects in 2025.

dorotheum.name: Dorotheum
dorotheum.what: An auction house founded in Vienna in 1707 by Emperor Joseph I; a state enterprise until its 2001 sale to Erwin and Hanno Soravia and Christoph Dichand.
dorotheum.money: Its auctions, retail sales and pawn lending; about 600 auctions a year bring some 60 percent of its turnover.

dowse.name: The Dowse Foundation
dowse.what: An independent charitable trust established in 2003 and registered in 2008 that raises money for The Dowse Art Museum in Lower Hutt, New Zealand.
dowse.money: Donations from members of its Major Art Fund and The Dowse Collectors Club, and from business and individual supporters.
dowse.arts: It supports the museum's programme and the growth of its collection of New Zealand visual arts and crafts.
dowse.address: 45 Laings Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010

dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.name: Département des Bouches-du-Rhône
dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.what: The departmental government of Bouches-du-Rhône in southern France, run by an elected departmental council presided over by Martine Vassal, seated in Marseille.
dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.money: The departmental budget its councillors adopted on 14 April 2026, with more than 1.6 billion euros, over 62 percent of spending, for social welfare.

drac.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles d'Occitanie
drac.what: The French Ministry of Culture's regional office for Occitanie, a state service with its seat at the Hôtel de Grave in Montpellier and a second site in Toulouse.
drac.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.
drac.address: Hôtel de Grave, 5 rue Salle-l'Évêque, 34000 Montpellier

dracgrandest.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles Grand Est
dracgrandest.what: The regional office of the French Ministry of Culture for Grand Est, under the regional prefect, seated in the Palais du Rhin in Strasbourg with sites in Metz and Châlons-en-Champagne.
dracgrandest.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.

dracledefrance.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles d'Île-de-France
dracledefrance.what: The Paris office of the French Ministry of Culture for the Île-de-France region.
dracledefrance.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.

dracnouvelleaquitaine.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles Nouvelle-Aquitaine
dracnouvelleaquitaine.what: A regional service of the French Ministry of Culture under the prefect of Nouvelle-Aquitaine, with its seat in Bordeaux and sites in Limoges and Poitiers.
dracnouvelleaquitaine.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.

dracpaca.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
dracpaca.what: The regional office of France's Ministry of Culture for Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, a decentralised state service under the regional prefect, based in Aix-en-Provence.
dracpaca.address: 23 boulevard du Roi René, 13617 Aix-en-Provence Cedex 1

drarthurmsackler.name: Arthur M. Sackler
drarthurmsackler.what: American psychiatrist, medical advertising executive and art collector (1913 to 1987), one of the three Sackler brothers; he died before Purdue began selling OxyContin.
drarthurmsackler.money: Medical advertising through the McAdams agency, bought in 1947, and the Medical Tribune, which he started in 1960; his estate was estimated at $140 million.
drarthurmsackler.arts: He paid for galleries at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, including the wing that houses the Temple of Dendur; the Met removed the Sackler name in December 2021.

dreweattsauctioneers.name: Dreweatts 1759 Limited
dreweattsauctioneers.what: An auction house established in 1759, with its main saleroom at Donnington Priory in Newbury, Berkshire, and a London showroom on Pall Mall; Gurr Johns controlled it until October 2026.
dreweattsauctioneers.money: Income from its auctions and from valuation services.

droomendaad.name: Stichting Droom en Daad
droomendaad.what: A family foundation set up in Rotterdam on 13 December 2016 by Martijn van der Vorm, former chief executive of the investment company HAL; Van der Vorms chair its board.
droomendaad.money: The Van der Vorm family fortune, invested in HAL since the family sold its Holland America cruise business in 1988.
droomendaad.arts: It takes no applications and develops its own Rotterdam projects through foundations it sets up, among them the Fenix museum.

droomendaadeur.name: Stichting Droom en Daad
droomendaadeur.what: A private foundation in Rotterdam, set up on 13 December 2016 by the Van der Vorm family to promote art and culture in the city.
droomendaadeur.money: The Van der Vorm family fortune, which began with the Holland America Line and grew through the investment company HAL.
droomendaadeur.arts: Its money helped build Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen, the Fenix museum and the reopened Nederlands Fotomuseum, and it takes no applications.

drosos.name: Drosos Stiftung
