koldingkommune|Denmark.what: The municipality of Kolding in the Region of Southern Denmark, formed by merger in the 2007 municipal reform, with 96,214 residents in 2026 and its town hall on Akseltorv.
koldingkommune|Denmark.money: The municipal budget of Kolding Kommune.

kolmont.name: Kolmont
kolmont.what: A Belgian property developer started as a family business in 2000, with offices in Hasselt and Brussels.
kolmont.money: Sales and lettings of the houses, apartments, building plots, shops and offices it develops.

kommuneqarfiksermersooq.name: Kommuneqarfik Sermersooq
kommuneqarfiksermersooq.what: The Greenland municipality with its seat in the capital Nuuk, formed on 1 January 2009 from five smaller municipalities; by area it is the largest municipality in the world.
kommuneqarfiksermersooq.money: Income tax: residents pay a 26% municipal rate and a 6% joint municipal tax, according to Greenland's Tax Agency.

koreahana.name: Korea Hana Foundation
koreahana.what: A South Korean public body set up by the Ministry of Unification in September 2010 under the act on settlement support for North Korean defectors; it helps them resettle.
koreahana.money: The South Korean government, as a quasi-government organisation of the Ministry of Unification since January 2011, plus public donations.

koret.name: Koret Foundation
koret.what: A private foundation in San Francisco set up in 1979 by Joseph Koret, who built the Koret of California apparel brand with his late wife Stephanie.
koret.money: Returns on its endowment: dividends, interest and asset sales; total assets were $287.4 million at the end of 2025, per its Form 990-PF.
koret.arts: Arts and culture is one of its grant areas; it has given more than $1 billion in grants since 1980.

kpbs.name: KPBS Public Media
kpbs.what: San Diego's public radio and television broadcaster, a department of San Diego State University, founded on the campus in 1960 as KEBS.
kpbs.money: Member donations and underwriting; federal grants of about $4.3 million a year, 12% of its $38.5 million budget, ended in 2025.

kpmg.name: KPMG International Limited
kpmg.what: A network of audit, tax and advisory member firms, formed in 1987 by the merger of Peat Marwick International and Klynveld Main Goerdeler; its coordinating company is in London.
kpmg.money: Fees its member firms earn for audit, tax and advisory work: combined revenue of US$38.4 billion in 2024.

kpn.name: Koninklijke KPN N.V.
kpn.what: The Dutch telecom company, corporatised from the state postal and telephone service PTT in 1989 and privatised from 1994; América Móvil holds 16.08 percent.
kpn.money: Telephone, internet, TV and IT services, mostly in the Netherlands: EUR 5.829 billion adjusted revenue in 2025.

krber.name: Körber-Stiftung
krber.what: A private foundation set up in Hamburg in 1959 by the businessman Kurt A. Körber; it is the sole shareholder of Körber AG, the holding of the Körber Group.
krber.money: An annual dividend from Körber AG; the foundation's assets are about €580 million.
krber.arts: Culture is one of its seven subject areas.

kuka.name: KUKA SE & Co. KGaA
kuka.what: A German robotics and automation company founded in Augsburg in 1898 by Johann Josef Keller and Jakob Knappich, wholly owned by China's Midea group since 2022.
kuka.money: Sales of industrial robots, automated production systems, intralogistics and healthcare automation; revenue was €3.9 billion in 2025.

kulka.name: Eesti Kultuurkapital
kulka.what: A legal person in public law that supports the arts, folk culture and sport in Estonia, established by law in 1925, re-established in 1994 and based in Tallinn.
kulka.money: By law, 3.5 percent of Estonia's alcohol and tobacco excise and 47.8 percent of its gambling tax.
kulka.arts: It gives grants, scholarships and awards through eight endowments, visual and applied arts among them.

kulturreferatoflandeshauptstadtmnchen.name: Kulturreferat der Landeshauptstadt München
kulturreferatoflandeshauptstadtmnchen.what: The department of Munich's city administration for arts and culture funding, in charge of the municipal museums, theatres and libraries.
kulturreferatoflandeshauptstadtmnchen.money: The budget of the City of Munich: about EUR 154.7 million for the department in 2025.

kulturstiftungdesbundes.name: Kulturstiftung des Bundes
kulturstiftungdesbundes.what: An independent foundation set up in 2002 with seat in Halle an der Saale that funds contemporary art and culture across Germany and abroad.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.money: German federal funds: an annual budget of 35 million euros.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.arts: Since 2002 it has run over 40 funding programmes and backed about 4,000 projects, with multi-year support for documenta and the Berliner Theatertreffen.

kulturstiftungkunsthallebielefeld.name: Kulturstiftung Kunsthalle Bielefeld
kulturstiftungkunsthallebielefeld.what: A charitable foundation in Bielefeld, set up in 1997 as Kulturstiftung Pro Bielefeld on the initiative of Wolfgang Böllhoff and recognised by the state on 7 May 1997.

kunsthallebern.name: Stiftung Kunsthalle Bern
kunsthallebern.what: A foundation in Bern founded in 1987 by Bernhard Hahnloser, Donald Hess, Paul Jolles, Beat Jordi and Eberhard W. Kornfeld to collect art shown at the Kunsthalle Bern.
kunsthallebern.arts: It buys works by artists shown at the Kunsthalle and lends them mainly to the Kunstmuseum Bern, and held about 400 works in 2016.
kunsthallebern.address: c/o Stiftung Kunstmuseum Bern, Hodlerstrasse 8-12, 3011 Bern

kunststiftungnrw.name: Kunststiftung NRW
kunststiftungnrw.what: A public-law foundation set up on 12 September 1989 by the North Rhine-Westphalia state government under Johannes Rau, based in the Haus der Stiftungen in Düsseldorf.
kunststiftungnrw.money: The proceeds of the lottery operator WestLotto.
kunststiftungnrw.arts: It has funded about 12,000 projects in literature, music, performing arts and visual art with a link to North Rhine-Westphalia since 1989.

kunststiftungvolkswagen.name: Kunststiftung Volkswagen
kunststiftungvolkswagen.what: A charitable foundation under civil law in Wolfsburg that operates the Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg.
kunststiftungvolkswagen.money: Most of its money comes from the Holler-Stiftung, set up in 1990 from the estate of Asta and Christian Holler, former owners of Volkswagen Versicherungsdienst.

kurabo.name: Kurabo Industries Ltd.
kurabo.what: A Japanese textile and chemicals group founded on 9 March 1888 as Kurashiki Spinning Works in Kurashiki, now headquartered in Osaka.
kurabo.money: Sales of textiles, chemical products, advanced technology equipment, food services and real estate.

kuraray.name: Kuraray Co., Ltd.
kuraray.what: A Japanese chemicals and fibre maker founded in Kurashiki in 1926 by Magosaburō Ōhara and Torajiro Kojima, with head offices in Tokyo and Osaka.
kuraray.money: Sales of chemicals, resins, synthetic fibres, high performance materials and dental materials; its main plants are in Kurashiki.

kuwaitpetroleum.name: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation
kuwaitpetroleum.what: Kuwait's state-owned oil company, founded on 27 January 1980 as the umbrella for KOC, KNPC, KOTC and PIC, headquartered in Kuwait City.
kuwaitpetroleum.money: Sales of Kuwait's crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals; revenue was KWD 30.06 billion in fiscal 2024/25.
kuwaitpetroleum.address: Oil Sector Complex, Shuwaikh Industrial 1, Block 1, Street 74, Kuwait

kyocera.name: Kyocera Corporation
kyocera.what: A Japanese ceramics and electronics manufacturer founded in Kyoto in 1959 by Kazuo Inamori as Kyoto Ceramic Company, renamed in 1982.
kyocera.money: Sales of industrial ceramics, semiconductor packages, electronic components, solar power systems and office printers; revenue was ¥1.58 trillion in 2018.
kyocera.arts: It runs the Kyocera Museum of Fine Ceramics and the Kyocera Gallery.

lacity|USA.name: City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs
lacity|USA.what: A department of the City of Los Angeles that makes grants to arts and cultural organisations and artists and manages the city's cultural programmes.
lacity|USA.money: By city code, an amount equal to 1% of expected hotel Transient Occupancy Tax revenue, plus Arts Development Fees paid on non-residential building projects.
lacity|USA.address: 201 North Figueroa Street, Suite 1400, Los Angeles, CA 90012

lambent.name: Lambent Foundation
lambent.what: A New York grantmaker for art, culture and social justice founded by the artist Anne Delaney, grown out of her Starry Night Fund of 2002.
lambent.money: Anne Delaney's philanthropy, held as a fiscally sponsored project of the Tides Center, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.
lambent.arts: It funds contemporary art and culture tied to social justice in New York City, New Orleans and Nairobi.
lambent.address: 55 Exchange Place, Suite 406, New York, NY 10005

lanacin.name: Gobierno de Colombia
lanacin.what: The national government of Colombia, a unitary presidential republic with its capital in Bogotá.

landberlin|Germany.name: Land Berlin
landberlin|Germany.what: The state government of Berlin: the Senate, led by the Governing Mayor (Der Regierende Bürgermeister) through the Senatskanzlei.
landberlin|Germany.money: The Berlin state budget passed by the Abgeordnetenhaus, about EUR 45.5 billion for 2026 and EUR 46.5 billion for 2027.
landberlin|Germany.arts: Its Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion has EUR 957.3 million in non-staff funds for 2026, down from EUR 1.026 billion in 2025.

landcareaustralia.name: Landcare Australia
landcareaustralia.what: An independent national not-for-profit for environmental conservation and sustainable land management, set up in 1989, when landcare became a national movement championed by Prime Minister Bob Hawke.
landcareaustralia.money: Grants from government partners, sponsorship from corporate partners and public donations.

landobersterreich|Austria.name: Land Oberösterreich
landobersterreich|Austria.what: The government of Upper Austria, one of Austria's nine states, run from the Amt der Oö. Landesregierung in Linz.
landobersterreich|Austria.money: The Upper Austrian state budget, about EUR 9.9 billion for 2026, planned with a deficit of about EUR 255 million.

landofsalzburg|Austria.name: Land Salzburg
landofsalzburg|Austria.what: A federal state (Land) of Austria with 561,714 inhabitants (2021 census), governed from the city of Salzburg; Governor Karoline Edtstadler heads its government.
landofsalzburg|Austria.money: The state budget: about EUR 4.5 billion for 2026, approved in the Salzburg Landtag on 26 November 2025.
landofsalzburg|Austria.arts: The 2026 budget gives EUR 105 million to art, culture and religious affairs (Kunst, Kultur und Kultus).

landvorarlberg|Austria.name: Amt der Vorarlberger Landesregierung
landvorarlberg|Austria.what: The administration of the government of the Austrian state of Vorarlberg, population 401,674, led by Landeshauptmann Markus Wallner (ÖVP) and seated in the Landhaus in Bregenz.
landvorarlberg|Austria.money: The state budget of Vorarlberg, which plans €2.8 billion in spending for 2026, including about €200 million in new borrowing.

langlois.name: Daniel Langlois Foundation for Art, Science, and Technology
langlois.what: A private charitable foundation set up in Montreal in 1997 by Daniel Langlois (1957 to 2023), the founder of the 3D animation software company Softimage.
langlois.money: Daniel Langlois's fortune from Softimage, the company he founded in 1986, which Microsoft bought for 130 million dollars in 1994.
langlois.arts: It supports artistic, scientific and technological research and keeps a documentation collection on electronic and media arts from the 1960s onward.

laskinfamily.name: Laskin Family Foundation, Inc.
laskinfamily.what: A private family foundation in Milwaukee, tax-exempt since March 1968; James P. Laskin is its president and William A. Laskin its vice president and treasurer.
laskinfamily.money: Contributions it receives: $10.5 million of its $10.9 million revenue in 2025 and $592,080 of $1.18 million in 2024.
laskinfamily.address: 833 E. Michigan St., Suite 1800, Milwaukee, WI 53202

latam.name: LATAM Airlines Group S.A.
latam.what: A Chilean airline holding company formed in 2012 when LAN Airlines took over Brazil's TAM Linhas Aéreas, headquartered in Santiago and listed in Santiago and New York.
latam.money: Passenger and cargo flights, with US$13.034 billion revenue in 2024; Sixth Street Partners, Delta Air Lines and Qatar Airways are its largest shareholders.

latrobeuniversity.name: La Trobe University
latrobeuniversity.what: A public research university in Victoria, Australia, established on 9 December 1964, with its main campus in Bundoora, Melbourne, and regional campuses.
latrobeuniversity.money: Government funding and student fees; its budget was A$863.7 million in 2023.

latvianministryofculture|Latvia.name: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Latvia
latvianministryofculture|Latvia.what: The Latvian state institution that organises and coordinates culture, social integration and media policy, based in Riga.

lazardfreresgestion.name: Fondation Lazard Frères Gestion-Institut de France
lazardfreresgestion.what: A foundation created in 2020 with the Institut de France by Lazard Frères Gestion, which is owned 99.99% by Compagnie Financière Lazard Frères.
lazardfreresgestion.money: Lazard Frères Gestion's asset management business in Paris; the firm has sponsored heritage projects since 2007.
lazardfreresgestion.arts: It paid for restoring Pierre Dulin's painting of the Hôtel Royal des Invalides, finished in March 2021, and supports four Institut National du Patrimoine students each year.

lazraqfamily.name: Alliances Développement Immobilier
lazraqfamily.what: A Moroccan property developer listed in Casablanca, founded by Alami Lazraq, who chairs it and controls 51.7 percent of its shares.
lazraqfamily.money: Sales of residential, commercial and tourism property developments across North Africa.
lazraqfamily.arts: Its cultural patronage covers the Fondation MACAAL, built on the art collection of Alami and Farida Lazraq, and a sculpture park.

lecorbusier.name: Fondation Le Corbusier
lecorbusier.what: A French foundation recognised as of public utility by decree on 24 July 1968, universal legatee of the architect Le Corbusier; its seat is the Maison Jeanneret, Paris.
lecorbusier.money: Le Corbusier left it everything he owned, including his archives and the moral and economic rights to all his works, which ADAGP manages.

leedscitycouncil|UK.name: Leeds City Council
leedscitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the City of Leeds in West Yorkshire, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, which meets at Leeds Civic Hall.
leedscitycouncil|UK.money: Council tax and UK government funding; for 2026/27 its government resources rose by £71.1m and council tax by 4.99 per cent.
leedscitycouncil|UK.address: Civic Hall, Calverley Street, Leeds LS1 1UR

leica.name: Leica Camera AG
leica.what: A German maker of cameras, lenses and optics in Wetzlar, with roots in Carl Kellner's Optical Institute of 1849; Andreas Kaufmann's ACM holds 55% and Blackstone 45%.
leica.money: Sales of cameras, lenses and other optical products; turnover was €596 million in 2024/25.
leica.arts: It runs about 30 Leica galleries and gives the Leica Oskar Barnack Award and the Leica Hall of Fame Award to photographers.

lendlease.name: Lendlease Corporation Limited
lendlease.what: An Australian property and construction group founded in Sydney in 1958 by Dick Dusseldorp, with its head office in the International Towers at Barangaroo.
lendlease.money: Property investment, development, construction and asset management: AUD 8.82 billion revenue in 2022.

leonblack.name: Leon Black
leonblack.what: An American private equity investor who co-founded Apollo Global Management in 1990 and was its CEO; he chaired the Museum of Modern Art from 2018 to 2021.
leonblack.money: His retained stake in Apollo Global Management; Bloomberg put his net worth at about US$13.8 billion in 2026.

lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.name: Les Amis des Musées d'art et d'histoire du Luxembourg a.s.b.l.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.what: A Luxembourg non-profit association of friends of six museums, under the patronage of the Grand Duchess, tracing its history to the Société des Amis des Musées founded in 1926.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.money: Members' subscriptions and donations; gifts and bequests can also go to its public-utility foundation, the Fondation des Amis des Musées.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.arts: It helps the museums acquire works, among them Jacques Monory's La terrasse no. 5 for the Musée national.

leventis.name: A. G. Leventis Foundation
leventis.what: A private foundation set up in May 1979 under provisions made by Anastasios G. Leventis, a Greek Cypriot trader in West Africa, with its executive office in Zurich.
leventis.money: The fortune Anastasios G. Leventis made with A. G. Leventis & Company, his West African trading group founded in 1936.
leventis.arts: Its own initiatives are the A. G. Leventis Gallery and the Leventis Municipal Museum, and it gives grants for heritage conservation, museums and libraries.

leverhulme.name: The Leverhulme Trust
leverhulme.what: A UK grant-making charity in London, established in 1925 under the will of the 1st Viscount Leverhulme to fund scholarships for research and education.
leverhulme.money: Its shareholding in Unilever plc, which began as shares in Lever Brothers; it gives out over £100 million a year.

lexus.name: Lexus
lexus.what: The luxury car division of the Japanese carmaker Toyota Motor Corporation, launched in 1989 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi.
lexus.money: Sales of Lexus cars within Toyota Motor Corporation, whose revenue was ¥48.04 trillion in 2025.

libbeys.name: Edward Drummond Libbey and Florence Scott Libbey
libbeys.what: Edward Drummond Libbey, owner of the Libbey Glass Company in Toledo, founded the Toledo Museum of Art in 1901 and led it until 1925; Florence Scott Libbey was his wife.
libbeys.money: Edward Libbey's fortune from Libbey Glass, the Owens Bottle Machine Company and Libbey-Owens Sheet Glass, given to the museum as the Libbey Endowment.
libbeys.arts: The Toledo Museum of Art still buys art from the Libbey Endowment, for example a Sasanian silver plate in 2022.
libbeys.renamed: The atlas name points at Libbey Glass, the company; the museum sentence means the funds the Libbeys themselves left to the museum.

libertyinnorthkorea.name: Liberty in North Korea
libertyinnorthkorea.what: A US nonprofit that rescues North Korean refugees hiding in China and resettles them, founded at Yale University on 27 March 2004 and registered in Long Beach, California.
libertyinnorthkorea.money: Donations, including money raised by school, college and church Rescue Teams: USD 4,214,232 in 2025.

liljestrand.name: Liljestrand Foundation
liljestrand.what: A Honolulu nonprofit, tax-exempt since 2008 and led by members of the Liljestrand family, that preserves the 1952 house Vladimir Ossipoff designed for Howard and Betty Liljestrand.
liljestrand.money: Gifts from the Friends of the Liljestrand Foundation and guided tour income, with revenue of $496,717 in 2023.

lilly.name: Lilly Endowment Inc.
lilly.what: A private foundation in Indianapolis, created in 1937 by J.K. Lilly Sr. and his sons Eli and J.K. Jr. through gifts of Eli Lilly and Company stock.
lilly.money: Its endowment, mostly Eli Lilly and Company stock; total assets were US$106 billion in 2025.

linbury.name: The Linbury Trust
linbury.what: A UK grant-making trust, one of the Sainsbury Family Charitable Trusts, set up by Lord Sainsbury of Preston Candover and the ballerina Anya Linden, first granting in 1973.
linbury.money: Investment income and donations; it held funds of £135.0 million at 5 April 2025.
linbury.arts: In the year to April 2025 it paid £3.7 million to culture, including £2.25 million to the National Gallery's Sainsbury Wing.
linbury.address: The Peak, 5 Wilton Road, London SW1V 1AP

lincolnfinancial.name: Lincoln National Corporation
lincolnfinancial.what: A US insurance and asset management company trading as Lincoln Financial Group, organised in Indiana in 1968 with roots in 1905, headquartered in Radnor, Pennsylvania.
lincolnfinancial.money: Premiums and fees from insurance and asset management, including group life, disability and dental cover; revenue was US$19.230 billion in 2021.

lindapaceendowment.name: Linda Pace Foundation
lindapaceendowment.what: A private foundation in San Antonio, founded in 2003 as owner and steward of the art collection of Linda Pace (1945 to 2007), founder of Artpace.
lindapaceendowment.money: The fortune of Linda Pace, whose parents owned Pace Foods, with total assets of $95,476,515 in 2024.
lindapaceendowment.arts: It runs the exhibition spaces Ruby City and Studio in San Antonio and lends works from its collection to museums.

linklaters.name: Fondation d'entreprise Linklaters
linklaters.what: The corporate foundation of the Paris office of the law firm Linklaters, created in 2015 and chaired by the competition partner Anne Wachsmann-Guigon.
linklaters.money: The law firm Linklaters LLP, headquartered in London, which reported revenues of £2.32 billion in the 2024-25 financial year.
linklaters.arts: It funds image-education programmes for young people at LE BAL in Paris; the Paris office has collected photography since 2010, beginning with Raymond Depardon.

linzagascorepartners.name: LINZ AG für Energie, Telekommunikation, Verkehr und Kommunale Dienste
linzagascorepartners.what: A utility holding company formed in October 2000 from the merger of ESG and Stadtbetriebe Linz, wholly owned by the City of Linz through its holding company.
linzagascorepartners.money: Energy supply, municipal services and public transport in Linz and 115 other municipalities: revenue of 1,182.8 million euros in the year to 30 September 2025.

littlegreene.name: The Little Greene Paint Company Limited
littlegreene.what: A British paint and wallpaper maker in Manchester, incorporated on 22 May 1996, founded by the chemist David Mottershead and run by him and his family.
littlegreene.money: Sales of house paint and wallpaper, with a factory in Wales.
littlegreene.arts: It has a partnership with the National Trust to develop designs from the Trust's collections.
littlegreene.address: The Coachworks, 420 Ashton Old Road, Openshaw, Manchester M11 2DT

littlesun.name: Little Sun
littlesun.what: A Berlin nonprofit founded in 2012 by the artist Olafur Eliasson and the engineer Frederik Ottesen to bring solar energy to off-grid communities in Africa.
littlesun.money: Donations, funder grants and sales of its solar products; Bloomberg Philanthropies made a US$5 million impact investment in 2014.

liuna.name: Laborers' International Union of North America
liuna.what: A trade union of construction and energy workers in the United States and Canada, founded in 1903 and headquartered in Washington, DC, with about half a million members.
liuna.money: Its 2024 US tax return reports US$111.0 million in revenue, 89.7% of it program service revenue and 6.4% investment income.

liuyiqian.name: Liu Yiqian
liuyiqian.what: A Chinese investor and art collector born in Shanghai in 1963, chairman of the Shanghai investment company Sunline Group and co-founder of the Long Museum with his wife Wang Wei.
liuyiqian.money: Investments since the mid-1980s in listed shares, real estate and pharmaceuticals, giving a net worth Forbes put at USD 1.37 billion in July 2015.

liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.name: Liverpool City Council
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Liverpool, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, under Labour control since 2010, with main offices in the Cunard Building.
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.money: Business rates (£295.1m), council tax (£277.0m) and general government grants (£245.5m) in its 2026-27 budget, £1.8bn gross.

llbean.name: L.L.Bean, Inc.
llbean.what: A privately held American retailer of clothing and outdoor equipment, founded in 1912 by Leon Leonwood Bean in Freeport, Maine, where it is still headquartered.
llbean.money: Sales of clothing, footwear and outdoor recreation equipment; revenue was US$1.7 billion in 2023.

localfirmssilson.name: Silson Limited
localfirmssilson.what: A private company in Southam, Warwickshire, established in 1994 to make thin membranes for X-ray microscopy.
localfirmssilson.money: Sales of silicon nitride and other thin membranes to more than 900 customers in 50 countries.
localfirmssilson.address: 1 Insight Park, Welsh Road East, Southam, Warwickshire CV47 1NE

lockheedmartin.name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
lockheedmartin.what: A US defence and aerospace manufacturer based in Bethesda, Maryland, formed on 15 March 1995 by the merger of the Lockheed Corporation with Martin Marietta.
lockheedmartin.money: US government contracts: 73 percent of its 2024 revenue came from the federal government, 65 percent from the Department of Defense.

lombardodier.name: Bank Lombard Odier & Co Ltd
lombardodier.what: A Geneva private bank founded on 11 January 1796, organised as a partnership limited by shares under six managing partners, with headquarters at 1Roof in Bellevue, Geneva.
lombardodier.money: Fees from wealth management, asset management and banking IT services; assets under management were CHF 349 billion in 2023.

lonablottery|Burkina Faso.name: Loterie Nationale Burkinabè
lonablottery|Burkina Faso.what: Burkina Faso's national lottery, created on 10 May 1967 by ordinance and a state-owned company (société d'État) since November 1994, based in Ouagadougou.
lonablottery|Burkina Faso.money: Sales of lottery tickets, PMU'B horse-race bets and other games; turnover grew from 30 million FCFA in 1967 to 110 billion FCFA in 2016.

lookgalapresentedbymawer.name: Mawer Investment Management Ltd.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.what: An independent, privately owned investment firm founded in Calgary in 1974 by Charles Mawer as Mawer & Associates.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.money: Fees for managing about C$64.0 billion for individual and institutional investors.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.arts: It pledges at least 1% of pre-tax profits to community causes, which include the arts, and reports more than C$2.5 million donated.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.address: 517 10th Avenue SW, Suite 600, Calgary, Alberta T2R 0A8

losangelescounty|USA.name: County of Los Angeles
losangelescounty|USA.what: A California county formed on 18 February 1850 and governed by an elected five-member Board of Supervisors, with an estimated 9,694,934 residents in 2025.
losangelescounty|USA.money: The county budget: USD 52.5 billion for 2025-26, as adopted by the Board of Supervisors on 30 September 2025.

loterieromande.name: Société de la loterie de la Suisse romande
loterieromande.what: A public-benefit lottery and sports betting company created in 1937 under an agreement between the governments of the French-speaking Swiss cantons, based in Lausanne; Jura joined in 1979.
loterieromande.money: Lottery and sports betting: gross gaming revenue was CHF 429.8 million in 2025, and its whole profit, CHF 252 million, went to associations.
loterieromande.arts: Its profit goes to associations in culture, social welfare, health, research, education, the environment, tourism, heritage and sport.

lotterywest.name: Lotterywest (Lotteries Commission of Western Australia)
lotterywest.what: Western Australia's state lottery operator, set up in 1932 as the Lotteries Commission of Western Australia and headquartered in Subiaco, Perth.
lotterywest.money: Profits from its lottery games, shared under the Lotteries Commission Act 1990 among health, sport, the arts and direct community grants.
lotterywest.arts: The Act sends 5% of profits to the Arts Lottery Account (as of 2013), and Lotterywest is a major supporter of the Perth Festival.

lottothringen|Germany.name: Thüringer Staatslotterie AöR
lottothringen|Germany.what: The state lottery of Thuringia, a public-law institution (Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts) of the Free State of Thuringia, seated in Suhl.
lottothringen|Germany.money: Players' stakes in the lotteries it runs in Thuringia under the 2021 State Treaty on Gambling.

louisartmuseum.name: St. Louis Art Museum Foundation
louisartmuseum.what: A nonprofit in St. Louis, tax exempt since September 1985, that supports a single organisation, the Saint Louis Art Museum, and has the museum's director as its president.
louisartmuseum.money: Contributions ($9,188,525), investment income ($8,962,571) and asset sales ($6,707,045) in 2025, on net assets of $356,767,694.

louishansen.name: Aage og Johanne Louis-Hansens Fond
louishansen.what: A Danish commercial foundation in Copenhagen, set up in 1969 by Johanne Louis-Hansen in memory of her husband Aage Louis-Hansen, founder of the ostomy products company Coloplast.
louishansen.money: Dividends on Coloplast shares: its subsidiary Aage og Johanne Louis-Hansen A/S holds 11 percent of the capital and 15 percent of the votes.
louishansen.arts: It gave an average of over 240 million kroner a year in 2019 to 2023, with art and culture the largest field by grants and amount.

louisroederer.name: Louis Roederer
louisroederer.what: A champagne house in Reims, founded in 1776 as Dubois Père & Fils, renamed by Louis Roederer in 1833 and still owned by his descendants, the Rouzaud family.
louisroederer.money: Sales of its champagnes, including Cristal, with over 3.5 million bottles shipped a year, and of wines from estates such as Château de Pez.
louisroederer.arts: Its Fondation Louis Roederer gives the Discovery Award at the Rencontres d'Arles photography festival.

louisvuitton.name: Louis Vuitton Malletier SAS
louisvuitton.what: A Paris fashion house founded in 1854 by Louis Vuitton, now a subsidiary of the luxury group LVMH.
louisvuitton.money: Sales of leather goods, shoes, watches, jewellery and other luxury products; revenue was €14 billion in 2020.
louisvuitton.arts: In 2006 it opened the Espace Louis Vuitton, an exhibition space on the seventh floor of its Champs-Élysées store in Paris.

loukil.name: Loukil Holding
loukil.what: A Tunisian family business group founded in 1976 by Mohamed Loukil, who died in 2023, and chaired by his son Bassem Loukil; it works through about 30 companies.
loukil.money: Its companies in agriculture, heavy industry and consulting, and its role as Tunisian representative of Mazda, Kubota, Panasonic, Mitsubishi and Samsung.

lucefdn.name: The Henry Luce Foundation
lucefdn.what: A private foundation formed in New York in 1936 by Henry R. Luce, co-founder of Time magazine and founder of Fortune and Life.
lucefdn.money: An endowment built from Henry R. Luce's stock in his publishing company, Time Inc., and his estate; total assets were US$1.09 billion in 2023.
lucefdn.arts: Its American Art Program, begun in 1980 with a US$4 million allocation as the Luce Fund for Scholarship in American Art, funds museum exhibitions and collection projects.

ludwig.name: Peter und Irene Ludwig Stiftung
ludwig.what: A foundation in Aachen set up in 1997 by Irene Ludwig, a year after the death of her husband Peter Ludwig, to place their collection in public museums.
ludwig.money: The fortune of Irene and Peter Ludwig, who ran the Monheim chocolate company until its sale in 1986, then Ludwig Schokolade until 1998.

luma.name: LUMA Foundation
luma.what: A Zurich non-profit set up in 2004 by Maja Hoffmann to support contemporary artists; it created the LUMA Arles arts campus, launched in 2013.
luma.money: Its founder Maja Hoffmann belongs to the shareholder pool of Roche founder descendants, which controls Roche Holding.

macallan.name: The Macallan
macallan.what: A single malt Scotch whisky distillery at Easter Elchies, Craigellachie, founded in 1824 by Alexander Reid and owned by Edrington, a private spirits company based in Glasgow.
macallan.money: Whisky sales, with all voting shares in its owner Edrington held by The Robertson Trust, a Scottish charity funded by the dividends.

maddocks.name: Maddocks
maddocks.what: An Australian law firm that began in Melbourne in 1885 as Maddock & Johnson, founded by Joe Maddocks and Arthur Johnson, with offices in Melbourne, Sydney and Canberra.
maddocks.money: Fees for legal work, from local government clients to construction, employment and commercial law; it has over 95 partners and 700 staff.
maddocks.address: Collins Square, Tower Two, Level 25, 727 Collins Street, Melbourne VIC 3008

madepossiblebylaurenz.name: Laurenz-Stiftung
madepossiblebylaurenz.what: A private foundation in Basel, set up in 1999 by Maja Oeri and her husband Hans U. Bodenmann in memory of their son Laurenz Jakob; it built and manages Schaulager.
madepossiblebylaurenz.money: The private fortune of Maja Oeri, granddaughter of Emanuel Hoffmann, whose father Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche founded the Roche pharmaceutical group in 1896.
madepossiblebylaurenz.arts: It gave CHF 50 million, half the cost, for the Kunstmuseum Basel extension opened in 2016, and funds two art history professorships at the University of Basel.

madridcitycouncil|Spain.name: Ayuntamiento de Madrid
madridcitycouncil|Spain.what: Madrid's city council, led by Mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida of the Partido Popular, with its main seat in the Palacio de Cibeles since November 2007.
madridcitycouncil|Spain.money: The city budget: EUR 6,578 million for 2026, approved by the council plenary on 22 December 2025.

madriddestino.name: Madrid Destino Cultura Turismo y Negocio, S.A.
madriddestino.what: A municipal public company that manages Madrid's cultural venues, tourism and events, created in 2013 by merging municipal companies and based at the Conde Duque cultural centre.

maes.name: Brouwerij Alken-Maes
maes.what: A Belgian brewery formed in 1988 by merging the Maes brewery at Kontich-Waarloos with Cristal-Alken at Alken; Heineken owns it.
maes.money: Beer sales under brands such as Maes pils, Cristal and Kronenbourg 1664.

mainzerstadtwerke.name: Mainzer Stadtwerke AG
mainzerstadtwerke.what: The municipal utility company of the City of Mainz, supplying electricity, gas, water and public transport, with stakes in about 50 companies.
mainzerstadtwerke.money: Sales of electricity, gas, water and public transport in Mainz and nearby towns; revenue was €508 million in 2019.
mainzerstadtwerke.arts: It set up and supports the Stiftung Kunsthalle Mainz and a Mainz foundation for climate protection and energy efficiency.

malaysiasstateoil|Malaysia.name: Petroliam Nasional Berhad
malaysiasstateoil|Malaysia.what: Malaysia's state oil and gas company, founded on 17 August 1974, owned by the Government of Malaysia and based in the Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur.
malaysiasstateoil|Malaysia.money: Oil, natural gas and petrochemicals, with revenue of US$73.01 billion in 2023.

malberln.name: Publikum.sk
malberln.what: An independent cultural centre in Trnava, Slovakia, opened in March 2018 and run by the civic association Publikum.sk, founded in 2009.
malberln.money: Public and EU project grants, among them the EU-financed Zmina.Rebuilding programme for Ukrainian culture, plus rentals of its spaces.

manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.name: Manchester City Council
manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Manchester in Greater Manchester, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, which meets at Manchester Town Hall on Albert Square.
manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.money: Its revenue budget, which passed £1 billion for the first time in 2026/27 as national government funding improved.
manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.address: Town Hall, Albert Square, Manchester M60 2LA

mandel.name: Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel Foundation
mandel.what: A private family foundation in Cleveland, Ohio; the brothers Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel set up their first charitable foundation in 1953.
mandel.money: The fortune the Mandel brothers made in Premier Industrial Corporation, which merged with Farnell Electronics in 1996 in a $3 billion deal.
mandel.arts: In 2026 it committed US$125 million to Case Western Reserve University, including a Mandel Humanities Building; its Boston institute runs a Cultural Leadership Program.

manitobaartscouncil|Canada.name: Manitoba Arts Council
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Province of Manitoba, established in 1965, that makes awards to professional artists and arts organisations through peer assessment.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.money: The Manitoba provincial budget, through the department of Sport, Culture, Heritage and Tourism.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.arts: Its budget was C$12.7 million in 2023.

manitobaliquor.name: Manitoba Liquor and Lotteries Corporation
manitobaliquor.what: A Crown corporation of the Province of Manitoba, established on 1 April 2014 under the Manitoba Liquor and Lotteries Corporation Act, based in Winnipeg.
manitobaliquor.money: Sales of liquor and gambling products, including casinos, VLTs and lottery tickets; it delivered C$724.1 million in profit to the Province of Manitoba in 2025-26.
manitobaliquor.arts: Its sponsorship and donation programmes totalled C$4.0 million in 2025-26.
manitobaliquor.address: Unit A, 1555 Buffalo Place, Winnipeg, Manitoba

mapei.name: Mapei S.p.A.
mapei.what: A maker of adhesives, sealants and chemical products for building, founded in Milan in 1937 by Rodolfo Squinzi; the Squinzi family holds 93.95 percent through Emme Esse Vi.
mapei.money: Sales of building chemicals: EUR 4.4 billion revenue in 2025.

mare.name: Fundația MARe
mare.what: A Bucharest foundation set up in February 2015 to run MARe, the Museum of Recent Art, Romania's first private museum of local art from the last five decades.
mare.money: The private money of its founder Roger Akoury, a Lebanese-born pharmaceutical entrepreneur, who funded the building and assembled its collection of around 550 works.

mariahofmanntrust.name: The Renate, Hans and Maria Hofmann Trust
mariahofmanntrust.what: A charitable trust created under the will of Renate Hofmann, widow of the painter Hans Hofmann, admitted to probate in New York County in 1996.
mariahofmanntrust.money: Sales of Hans Hofmann works it holds, through Miles McEnery Gallery, and investment dividends, with net assets of US$37,174,956 in June 2025.
mariahofmanntrust.arts: It supports exhibitions, publications and education on Hofmann's art and, under the will, gives to the Association of German Dioceses for people in need.

marinabaysands.name: Marina Bay Sands
marinabaysands.what: A casino resort on Marina Bay in Singapore, owned by Las Vegas Sands and opened in 2010, with a casino, a 1,850-room hotel and a convention centre.
marinabaysands.money: Its casino, hotel, convention and retail business.

maritimeelectric.name: Maritime Electric
maritimeelectric.what: An electric utility serving Prince Edward Island, founded in 1918, headquartered in Charlottetown and owned by Fortis Inc.
maritimeelectric.money: Electricity sales to about 92,000 customers, at rates regulated by the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission.

marriott.name: Marriott International, Inc.
marriott.what: A US hotel company headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland, formed in 1993 as successor to the hospitality arm of the Marriott Corporation founded by J. Willard and Alice Marriott.
marriott.money: Operating, franchising and licensing hotel, residential and timeshare brands; revenue was US$26.2 billion in 2025.

marwanassaf.name: Marwan T. Assaf
marwanassaf.what: A board member of the Beirut Art Center and a trustee of the Sursock Museum in Beirut.

massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.name: Mass Cultural Council
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.what: The public arts funding body of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, based in Boston, which makes grants to cultural organizations, schools, communities and individual artists.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.money: An annual appropriation from the Massachusetts Legislature, plus funds from the National Endowment for the Arts.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.address: 10 St. James Avenue, 3rd Floor, Boston, MA 02116-3803

mazda.name: Mazda Motor Corporation
mazda.what: A Japanese carmaker founded on 30 January 1920 as Toyo Cork Kogyo by Jujiro Matsuda, headquartered in Fuchu, Hiroshima Prefecture.
mazda.money: Sales of cars and commercial vehicles: net sales of 4,918.2 billion yen in the year to March 2026.

mbhbank.name: MBH Bank Nyrt.
mbhbank.what: A Hungarian bank formed on 1 May 2023 by merging MKB Bank, Takarékbank and Budapest Bank; Lőrinc Mészáros holds almost half the shares and the state-owned Corvinus 15%.
mbhbank.money: Interest and fees from banking in Hungary; net income was HUF 165.109 billion in 2025.

mcommemutuelle.name: M comme Mutuelle
mcommemutuelle.what: A French mutual health insurer founded in 1870 and built up through mergers of local mutuals, headquartered in Lille with agencies across northern France and Normandy.
mcommemutuelle.money: Contributions from individual members and employer clients for its health and provident (prévoyance) insurance.

meadows.name: The Meadows Foundation
meadows.what: A Dallas foundation set up in 1948 by the oilman Algur H. Meadows and his wife Virginia to benefit the people of Texas.
meadows.money: An endowment from Algur Meadows's fortune in General American Oil Company of Texas, sold to Phillips Petroleum in 1983; assets $694 million in 2023.

memoriav.name: Memoriav, Verein zur Erhaltung des audiovisuellen Kulturgutes der Schweiz
memoriav.what: A Swiss non-profit association for preserving audiovisual heritage, founded in Bern on 1 December 1995 by institutions including the National Library and the Federal Archives.

mendeswooddm.name: Mendes Wood DM
mendeswooddm.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded in São Paulo in 2010 by Pedro Mendes, Matthew Wood and Felipe Dmab, with further spaces in Brussels, Paris and New York.
mendeswooddm.money: Sales of work by the artists it represents.

mercator.name: Stiftung Mercator GmbH
mercator.what: A private foundation in Essen, run as a non-profit company, founded in 1996 by the Schmidt family of Duisburg, founders of the Metro wholesale group.
mercator.money: Donations from the Meridian Stiftung and the Cambiata Stiftung, which hold the Schmidt family's assets.
mercator.arts: It approved about EUR 58.5 million for 108 new projects in 2024.

merciervanlanschot.name: Mercier Van Lanschot
merciervanlanschot.what: The Belgian branch of the Dutch private bank Van Lanschot Kempen NV, trading under this name since January 2024 after Van Lanschot Belgium and Mercier Vanderlinden combined.
merciervanlanschot.money: Wealth management for clients with €10.5 billion of assets under management (third quarter 2023), run for its parent Van Lanschot Kempen.

mercisbv.name: Mercis bv
mercisbv.what: An Amsterdam company set up by the designer Pieter Brattinga for Dick Bruna, which since 1971 has managed the worldwide rights to his illustrations, Miffy (nijntje) among them.
mercisbv.money: Licensing of Dick Bruna's illustrations for products, and his Dutch books through Mercis Publishing bv since 1995.

merian.name: Christoph Merian Stiftung
merian.what: A public-law foundation in Basel created by the 1857 will of Christoph Merian (1800 to 1858), active since 3 May 1886 under the supervision of the Bürgergemeinde der Stadt Basel.
merian.money: Income from CHF 1.8 billion of yield assets in 2025, made up of rental property, building leases and an equity fund.

merribekcouncil|Australia.name: Merri-bek City Council
merribekcouncil|Australia.what: The local council for the City of Merri-bek in Melbourne's inner north, created as the City of Moreland in 1994 and renamed in September 2022, with its seat in Coburg.
merribekcouncil|Australia.money: Property rates, capped by the Victorian government; rates were set to raise A$202,778,329 for 2025-26.

methanexalso.name: Methanex Corporation
methanexalso.what: A methanol producer headquartered in Vancouver, incorporated in 1992 when it split off from Ocelot, with plants in Canada, Chile, Egypt, New Zealand, Trinidad and Tobago and the US.
methanexalso.money: Sales of methanol, plus ammonia and other products; revenue was US$3.6 billion in 2025.

metrobank.name: Metropolitan Bank & Trust Company
metrobank.what: A Philippine universal bank founded in Binondo, Manila, in 1962, with George Ty as founder, now headquartered at Metrobank Center in Taguig.
metrobank.money: Its banking business; GT Capital Holdings owns 39.8% and the Ty family and related parties 12.3%, with 47.8% public (June 2026).

miamidadecounty|USA.name: Miami-Dade County
miamidadecounty|USA.what: A county in southeast Florida with its seat in Miami, led by Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and a 13-member Board of County Commissioners.

miamidesigndistrict.name: Miami Design District Associates
miamidesigndistrict.what: A partnership of Craig Robins's company Dacra and L Catterton Real Estate, a fund set up in 2016 by Catterton, LVMH and Groupe Arnault, that develops Miami's Design District.

michaelaudain.name: Michael Audain
michaelaudain.what: A Canadian home builder and art collector, born in 1937, chairman since 1992 and a major shareholder of Polygon Homes Ltd. in Vancouver.

michaelotto.name: Michael Otto

middlesbroughcouncil|UK.name: Middlesbrough Council

mikekelleyforarts.name: Mike Kelley Foundation for the Arts

millhouse.name: Millhouse LLC

miltonkeynescouncil|UK.name: Milton Keynes City Council
miltonkeynescouncil|UK.what: The unitary authority for Milton Keynes, England, created on 1 April 1974 as a borough council and renamed after the borough won city status on 15 August 2022.

minalbajaj.name: Minal Bajaj

ministryofcultureczechrepublic|Czech Rep.name: Ministerstvo kultury České republiky

mittelbrandenburgischesparkasse.name: Mittelbrandenburgische Sparkasse in Potsdam
