omk.name: АО «Объединённая металлургическая компания»
omk.what: A Moscow steel pipe maker with five plants between Moscow and the Urals, including the Vyksa Steel Works; under UK sanctions since May 2023 and US sanctions since September 2023.
omk.money: Sales of steel pipes, pipeline valves and fittings, railway wheels and automotive springs.

omkuchastie.name: Благотворительный фонд поддержки семьи, защиты детства, материнства и отцовства «ОМК-Участие»
omkuchastie.what: A charitable foundation founded in 2008 on the initiative of Irina and Anatoly Sedykh; Irina Sedykh chairs its board of trustees and its general director works in Moscow.
omkuchastie.money: OMK, a private Moscow steel company fully controlled by Anatoly Sedykh, with revenue of 169.7 billion rubles in 2020.
omkuchastie.arts: It works in five regions, Vyksa among them, on culture, art and education for local communities beside direct aid to families.

omvzukunftspartner.name: OMV Aktiengesellschaft
omvzukunftspartner.what: Austria's integrated oil and gas company, founded on 3 July 1956 as Österreichische Mineralölverwaltung; the state holding ÖBAG owns 31.5% and Abu Dhabi's ADNOC 24.9%.
omvzukunftspartner.money: Sales of oil, natural gas, fuels and petrochemicals: revenue €24.3 billion and net income €1.52 billion in 2025.

onassis.name: Alexander S. Onassis Public Benefit Foundation
onassis.what: A private foundation set up in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, in 1975 under the will of the shipowner Aristotle Onassis, in memory of his son Alexander.
onassis.money: Profits of the Onassis Business Foundation, its holding for maritime transport and real estate, formed from half of Aristotle Onassis's estate.
onassis.arts: It endows Greek studies chairs at universities and runs Onassis USA, its New York affiliate based in the Olympic Tower on Fifth Avenue.

ontarioartscouncil|Canada.name: Ontario Arts Council
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Ontario government, created by provincial law in 1963 under Premier John Robarts; based in Toronto.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.money: The Government of Ontario, through its culture ministry.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.arts: It runs more than fifty funding programmes for Ontario artists and arts organisations.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.address: 121 Bloor Street East, 7th Floor, Toronto, ON M4W 3M5

opec.name: OPEC Fund for International Development
opec.what: An intergovernmental development finance institution set up on 28 January 1976 by the member states of OPEC; based in Vienna.
opec.money: Capital contributions from its member countries, plus bonds issued on capital markets under its Strategic Framework 2030.

opensociety.name: Open Society Foundations
opensociety.what: A grantmaking network founded by investor George Soros, begun with a Budapest foundation in 1984; the Open Society Institute was set up in New York in 1993.
opensociety.money: George Soros's personal fortune: he had given over $32 billion by 2017, including an $18 billion transfer announced that year.

oprahwinfreycharitable.name: Oprah Winfrey Charitable Foundation
oprahwinfreycharitable.what: A private foundation in Los Angeles with the television host Oprah Winfrey as trustee; tax-exempt since August 2010.
oprahwinfreycharitable.money: Gifts in some years ($35.2 million in 2018, $14.3 million in 2020) and investment income; net assets were $171.1 million at the end of 2024.

optus.name: Singtel Optus Pty Limited
optus.what: Australia's second-largest telecom company, owned by Singtel of Singapore; it grew from the satellite operator AUSSAT (1981) and gained a carrier licence in 1991.
optus.money: Mobile, home internet and fixed-line fees from over 10.7 million mobile customers: revenue A$8.05 billion in fiscal 2023.

oregoncommunity.name: Oregon Community Foundation
oregoncommunity.what: A statewide community foundation founded in 1973, with headquarters in Portland and offices in Baker City, Bend, Eugene, Medford and Salem.
oregoncommunity.money: Charitable funds set up by individuals, families, businesses and organisations: an endowment of US$3.02 billion in 2024, when it made $174 million in grants.
oregoncommunity.arts: Its Creative Heights Initiative funds Oregon arts and culture projects, with $1 million invested through its 2023 round.

orf.name: Österreichischer Rundfunk
orf.what: Austria's national public broadcaster, launched on 1 August 1955 and run from the ORF-Zentrum in Vienna.
orf.money: The ORF-Beitrag, a levy set by law on every Austrian address with an adult resident, plus limited on-air advertising.

orfnamedwertinvest.name: WertInvest Beteiligungsverwaltungs GmbH
orfnamedwertinvest.what: A Vienna real estate developer founded and owned by Michael Tojner, which has built projects in Austria, Germany and New York since 1993.
orfnamedwertinvest.money: Real estate development across housing, offices, hotels and industrial sites.

orkneyislandscouncil|UK.name: Orkney Islands Council
orkneyislandscouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the Orkney Islands, one of Scotland's 32 council areas, established in 1975 under the Local Government (Scotland) Act 1973 and based in Kirkwall.
orkneyislandscouncil|UK.money: A Scottish Government grant of £120,130,000, about 78% of its 2026/27 budget, plus council tax, service charges and its reserves.

osgf.name: Open Society Georgia Foundation
osgf.what: A Tbilisi grant-making foundation in the Open Society Foundations network since 1994, registered in Georgia in 1998; from 2024 its work continues as the Civil Society Foundation.
osgf.money: Grants from the Open Society network's Foundation Open Society Institute and Foundation to Promote Open Society, plus other donors.

oslocollectorsvenke.name: Venke and Rolf Hoff
oslocollectorsvenke.what: Norwegian art collectors who acquired the KaviarFactory building in Henningsvær, Lofoten, after the cannery closed in 2006 and turned it into a contemporary art space.
oslocollectorsvenke.money: Rolf Hoff's business, which makes signage and produces works for artists.
oslocollectorsvenke.arts: They have lent works to Tate Britain, Garage in Moscow and most Norwegian contemporary art museums, and support artist-run galleries in Oslo.

otpbank.name: OTP Bank Nyrt.
otpbank.what: Hungary's largest commercial bank, established as OTP Bank on 1 March 1949 with roots in the First National Savings Bank of Pest of 1839; chaired by Sándor Csányi.
otpbank.money: Banking profits from retail and corporate clients in Hungary and subsidiaries across Central and Eastern Europe and Central Asia, such as Bulgaria's DSK Bank.

outset.name: Outset Contemporary Art Fund
outset.what: A London arts charity established in 2003 and co-founded by Candida Gertler, registered as charity 1101476, one of an international network of independent Outset charities.
outset.money: Donations pooled from its patrons, with income of £327,947 in the year ending 31 December 2025.
outset.arts: The Outset network says it has distributed over £17 million since 2003 to more than 400 public art institutions.

owsleybrowniii.name: Owsley Brown III
owsleybrowniii.what: A documentary film director and producer from Louisville, Kentucky, founder of Magnanimus Wine Group in 2005 and son of Owsley Brown II, Brown-Forman's chief executive from 1993 to 2005.
owsleybrowniii.money: His wine business and the family wealth of the Browns, who have run the spirits company Brown-Forman since 1870.
owsleybrowniii.arts: His films include Night Waltz, on Paul Bowles, which won an Independent Spirit Award in 2000, and Music Makes a City, on the Louisville Orchestra.

oxfaminternacional.name: Stichting Oxfam International
oxfaminternacional.what: The secretariat of a confederation of over 20 independent Oxfam organisations, formed in 1995 as a Dutch foundation, Stichting Oxfam International, with headquarters in Nairobi.
oxfaminternacional.money: Institutional grants and public fundraising across the confederation, which reported total income of €1,009 million in 2023/24.
oxfaminternacional.address: ACS Plaza, Lenana Road, Kilimani, Nairobi

paiko.name: Paiko
paiko.what: A botanical boutique in Kaka'ako, Honolulu, founded by Tamara Rigney and owned by Courtney Monahan, which moved from Auahi Street to Halekauwila Street in 2023.
paiko.money: Sales of houseplants, cut flowers and pots from its shop.

paizretailfamily.name: Paiz family
paizretailfamily.what: A Guatemalan business family; in 1928 Salvador Paiz's grandfather founded what became the Almacenes Paiz chain and later Walmart Centroamérica.
paizretailfamily.money: Retail: the Almacenes Paiz stores, later part of Walmart Centroamérica; Salvador Paiz now chairs the investment company Grupo PDC.
paizretailfamily.arts: The family's Fundación Paiz runs the Bienal de Arte Paiz, held since 1978.

palmacouncil|Spain.name: Ajuntament de Palma
palmacouncil|Spain.what: The municipal government of Palma, Mallorca, a city of 438,234 people in 2024, led by mayor Jaime Martínez Llabrés of the People's Party.
palmacouncil|Spain.money: The city's municipal budget, set at €626.67 million for 2026 and approved by the council in December 2025.

paribu.name: Paribu Kripto Varlık Alım Satım Platformu A.Ş.
paribu.what: A crypto asset exchange based in Istanbul, founded in 2017 by Yasin Oral, who owns it outright and runs it as chief executive.
paribu.money: Its crypto trading and custody business, which reported daily trading volume above US$1 billion in February 2021.

partnersincludeafricanculture.name: African Culture Fund
partnersincludeafricanculture.what: A pan-African non-profit trust set up in Bamako in February 2018 by African artists and cultural actors, registered in Mali under a headquarters agreement.
partnersincludeafricanculture.money: Contributions from African artists and cultural actors, and grants from DOEN, the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, the Ford Foundation and Open Society Foundations.
partnersincludeafricanculture.arts: It finances artistic projects across Africa through calls for projects and trains cultural managers through its ACF Academy.

patio.name: Fondation Simón I. Patiño
patio.what: A Swiss foundation registered in Geneva in December 1958 to help Bolivian students and professors and to support cultural, social and ecological work in Bolivia.
patio.money: A fund of US$10 million set up when the Bolivian Patiño foundation ran short of money; the Patiño wealth came from Bolivian tin mining.
patio.arts: Its statutes include topping up the resources of the Fundación Universitaria Simón I. Patiño, created in Bolivia in 1931, and supporting literary and music prizes.

patriciagurdin.name: Patricia Gurdián de Ortiz
patriciagurdin.what: An art collector from León, Nicaragua, who founded the Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián in 1996 with Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga to promote the country's cultural development.
patriciagurdin.money: Grupo Promerica, the financial group of her co-founder, whose bank Banpro also supports the foundation's Managua art centre.
patriciagurdin.renamed: The atlas files her under Banpro, but the museum sentence names her as a founder of the Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián, not as the bank.

patronatodeartecontemporneo.name: Patronato de Arte Contemporáneo, A. C.
patronatodeartecontemporneo.what: A non-profit civil association in Mexico City that began in 2000 on the initiative of Magda Carranza, Osvaldo Sánchez and Patricia Sloane to finance contemporary art in Mexico.
patronatodeartecontemporneo.money: Contributions from its group of patrons, who join a patrons’ programme of visits, trips and seminars.
patronatodeartecontemporneo.arts: It finances non-profit contemporary art projects and has held the SIT_AC international theory symposium since 2002.
patronatodeartecontemporneo.address: Av. Paseo de las Palmas 820, piso 3, Lomas de Chapultepec, Miguel Hidalgo, 11000 CDMX

patronatopageshowsinterceramic.name: Internacional de Cerámica, S.A.B. de C.V.
patronatopageshowsinterceramic.what: A Mexican maker of ceramic and porcelain tiles and bath and kitchen products, founded in Chihuahua in 1978 by Óscar Almeida Chabre.
patronatopageshowsinterceramic.money: Sales of floor and wall tiles from plants in Chihuahua, Guanajuato and Garland, Texas, through showrooms and franchises in Mexico and abroad.

paulgettytrust.name: J. Paul Getty Trust
paulgettytrust.what: A trust founded in 1953 by J. Paul Getty, founder of Getty Oil, that runs the Getty Museum, Research Institute, Conservation Institute and Getty Foundation in Los Angeles.
paulgettytrust.money: An endowment of US$9.4 billion (2025) built on Getty's bequest, which included nearly $660 million in Getty Oil stock received in 1982.
paulgettytrust.arts: The Getty Foundation gives grants to museums and cultural institutions worldwide.

paulhamlyn.name: Paul Hamlyn Foundation
paulhamlyn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity started by publisher Paul Hamlyn in 1987 and in its current form since 2004; based in King's Cross, London.
paulhamlyn.money: An endowment from Paul Hamlyn's publishing fortune: a £50m gift in 1987 and about £308 million from his estate in 2001.
paulhamlyn.arts: It funds children and young people, with a focus on the arts.

paulramsay.name: Paul Ramsay Foundation
paulramsay.what: A private philanthropic foundation in Sydney, founded in 2006 by Paul Ramsay, who started the private hospital company Ramsay Health Care in 1964.
paulramsay.money: A bequest of A$3 billion from Paul Ramsay, who died in 2014 and left most of his estate to the foundation.
paulramsay.address: Yirranma Place, 262 Liverpool Street, Darlinghurst NSW 2010

paulsmith.name: Paul Smith Limited
paulsmith.what: A British fashion company founded in Nottingham in 1970 by the designer Sir Paul Smith, its majority shareholder, with Itochu holding 40%.
paulsmith.money: Sales of clothing, footwear, eyewear and accessories through 130 shops in more than 60 countries and online.
paulsmith.address: The Poplars, Lenton Lane, Nottingham NG7 2PW

paypal.name: PayPal Holdings, Inc.
paypal.what: An American online payments company based in San Jose, California, formed in March 2000 by the merger of Confinity and X.com and independent of eBay since 2015.
paypal.money: Fees on payments it handles for consumers and businesses, with revenue of US$33.2 billion in 2025.
paypal.wrong_match: The museum sentence names PayPal as the channel its donors pay through, not as a funder.

paysdemontbliardagglomration.name: Pays de Montbéliard Agglomération
paysdemontbliardagglomration.what: The intercommunal authority of 73 communes around Montbéliard in the Doubs, a communauté d'agglomération since 1999, in its present form since 1 January 2017.
paysdemontbliardagglomration.money: Local taxes on households and businesses within a total 2026 budget of €214 million, voted on 22 January 2026.

pellerestates.name: Andrew Peller Limited
pellerestates.what: A Canadian wine producer listed in Toronto and based in Grimsby, Ontario, whose brands include Peller Estates; in June 2026 it agreed to be bought by Fairfax Financial.
pellerestates.money: Sales of wine, ciders and spirits, including through 101 company stores in Ontario; revenue was C$393.0 million in the year to 31 March 2026.

penguin.name: Penguin Books Limited
penguin.what: A British publishing house founded in 1935 by Allen Lane with his brothers Richard and John, since 2013 an imprint of Penguin Random House.
penguin.money: Sales of books, with its parent Penguin Random House owned by the German media group Bertelsmann.

pepsico.name: PepsiCo, Inc.
pepsico.what: An American food and drinks company formed in 1965 by the merger of the Pepsi-Cola Company and Frito-Lay, with headquarters in Purchase, in Harrison, New York.
pepsico.money: Sales of food and drinks in more than 200 countries, with revenue of US$93.9 billion in fiscal 2025.

perarte.name: PerArte Stiftung
perarte.what: A Swiss foundation initiated in 2025 by Marianne and Martin Haefner and entered in the Zurich commercial register in May 2026 to fund major exhibitions at the Kunsthaus Zürich.
perarte.money: A start capital of CHF 30 million from the Haefner family.

petronor.name: Petróleos del Norte, S.A.
petronor.what: A Spanish oil refining company established on 30 November 1968, based in Muskiz in the Basque Country and owned by Repsol (85.98%) and Kutxabank (14.02%).
petronor.money: Refining at Muskiz, which the company calls Spain's largest refinery at 12 million tonnes a year, with over a third of output exported.

pewcharitabletrusts.name: The Pew Charitable Trusts
pewcharitabletrusts.what: A nonprofit based in Philadelphia, formed from seven trusts that the four children of Sun Oil founder Joseph N. Pew created between 1948 and 1979.
pewcharitabletrusts.money: The Sun Oil fortune of the Pew family, with the seven trusts holding assets of $6 billion as of 2020.
pewcharitabletrusts.arts: It supports civic and cultural projects in Philadelphia.

phillips.name: Phillips
phillips.what: An auction house founded in London in 1796, with head offices in London and New York and a UK holding company, Phillips Assets Ltd.
phillips.money: Fees on auction and private sales (UK turnover £89m in 2024), under a parent, Mercury Group Trading, controlled by Leonid Fridlyand and Leonid Strunin.

pierides.name: Pierides Foundation
pierides.what: A non-profit cultural foundation of the Pierides family, set up in 1974 and based in Larnaca, with a branch in Athens.
pierides.money: The Pierides family of Larnaca, whose businesses included shipping from 1860, banking from 1866 and insurance from 1872.
pierides.arts: It keeps the Pierides Museum in Larnaca under a trust with Bank of Cyprus and lists eight museums and collections in Cyprus and Athens.

pinakothekdermoderne.name: Stiftung Pinakothek der Moderne
pinakothekdermoderne.what: A foundation in Munich established in 1994 to collect private donations for building the Pinakothek der Moderne.
pinakothekdermoderne.money: Private donations, endowment gifts and bequests.
pinakothekdermoderne.arts: It funds education work at the museum and co-financed the Schaustelle, a temporary space for experiments.

pinault.name: Artémis
pinault.what: The Pinault family's holding company, founded in Paris in 1992 by François Pinault and chaired by his son François-Henri Pinault since 2003.
pinault.money: Its holdings, chiefly 42.3% of the luxury group Kering, plus Christie's, Château Latour and other wine estates, Creative Artists Agency and Ponant cruises.
pinault.arts: It backs the Pinault Collection, which opened the Bourse de Commerce in Paris in 2021.

pinchuks.name: Victor Pinchuk Foundation
pinchuks.what: The private philanthropic foundation of the Ukrainian businessman Victor Pinchuk, who consolidated his giving under it in 2006.
pinchuks.money: The fortune of Victor Pinchuk, founder of the pipe, railway wheel and steel producer Interpipe and of the investment firm EastOne Group.
pinchuks.arts: Through PinchukArtCentre it awards the Future Generation Art Prize, $100,000 every two years for artists under 35, announced in December 2009.

pipertrust.name: Virginia G. Piper Charitable Trust
pipertrust.what: A private foundation in Phoenix that Virginia Galvin Piper, widow of the Motorola founder Paul V. Galvin, established in 1995 to fund nonprofits in Maricopa County, Arizona.
pipertrust.money: About $600 million received from Virginia Piper's estate in 2000, held as an invested endowment.
pipertrust.arts: Arts and culture is one of its six programme areas, and its AGILE project builds the capacity of mid-sized arts organisations.

pirellionly.name: Pirelli & C. S.p.A.
pirellionly.what: An Italian tyre maker founded in Milan in 1872 by Giovanni Battista Pirelli, listed on the Borsa Italiana and headquartered in the city's Bicocca district.
pirellionly.money: Sales of tyres for cars, motorcycles and bicycles, with revenues of 6.8 billion euros in 2025.
pirellionly.arts: It established and supports Pirelli HangarBicocca, a non-profit foundation for contemporary art whose exhibitions are free of charge.

platinumbarjeel.name: Barjeel Art Foundation
platinumbarjeel.what: A non-profit art foundation in Sharjah, set up in 2010 by the Emirati writer and collector Sultan Sooud Al Qassemi to manage and show his collection of modern Arab art.
platinumbarjeel.money: It holds the personal collection of its founder, a member of Sharjah's ruling Al Qasimi family and chairman of the brokerage Barjeel Geojit Securities.
platinumbarjeel.arts: Since 2018 it has shown its collection in a long-term exhibition at the Sharjah Art Museum under a contract with the Sharjah Museums Authority.
platinumbarjeel.address: Al Saud Head Office Building, Level 2, Block B, Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Road, Muwailih Commercial, Sharjah

plenitude.name: Eni Plenitude S.p.A. Società Benefit
plenitude.what: An Italian energy company and Società Benefit controlled by Eni, registered in Milan and active in more than 15 countries.
plenitude.money: Energy sold to over 11 million European customers and power from about 6 GW of renewables; pro forma EBITDA about €1.1 billion in 2025.

plymouthcitycouncil|UK.name: Plymouth City Council
plymouthcitycouncil|UK.what: Plymouth's city council in Devon, England, a unitary authority since 1 April 1998, with 57 councillors meeting at the Council House on Armada Way.
plymouthcitycouncil|UK.money: A revenue budget of GBP 253.4 million for 2025/26: other grants 39 percent, council tax 24 percent, core government grants 16 percent.
plymouthcitycouncil|UK.address: Ballard House, West Hoe Road, Plymouth

pnc.name: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc.
pnc.what: A US bank holding company in Pittsburgh, tracing to the Pittsburgh Trust and Savings Company of 1845 and formed as PNC by a 1982 merger.
pnc.money: Interest and fees from personal, small business and corporate banking through PNC Bank; revenue was US$21.49 billion in 2023.

polishcultureministry|UK.name: Ministerstwo Kultury i Dziedzictwa Narodowego
polishcultureministry|UK.short: Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage
polishcultureministry|UK.what: Poland's government ministry for culture and national heritage, based in the Potocki Palace in Warsaw; Marta Cienkowska has been minister since 24 July 2025.

polishministryofculture|Poland.name: Ministerstwo Kultury i Dziedzictwa Narodowego
polishministryofculture|Poland.short: Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage
polishministryofculture|Poland.what: The Polish government ministry for culture and heritage, formed in its present shape on 31 October 2005, with its seat in the Potocki Palace in Warsaw.
polishministryofculture|Poland.money: The Polish state budget, with an annual ministry budget of PLN 4.029 billion.

polygonhomes.name: Polygon Homes Ltd.
polygonhomes.what: A Metro Vancouver home builder in business since 1980, chaired by its major shareholder Michael Audain.
polygonhomes.money: Sales of the homes it builds and develops, more than 35,000 to date, from masterplanned communities to high-rise towers.
polygonhomes.address: Suite 900-1333 West Broadway, Vancouver, BC V6H 4C2

pon.name: Pon Holdings B.V.
pon.what: A family-owned Dutch mobility group founded in 1980 by Ben Pon Jr., whose father became the Dutch Volkswagen importer in 1947, with headquarters in Amsterdam.
pon.money: Car importing and bicycle making, with total revenue of €9.9 billion in 2024, €2.1 billion of it from bicycles.

porscheholdingsalzburg.name: Porsche Holding Gesellschaft m.b.H.
porscheholdingsalzburg.what: A car distributor in Salzburg, grown from the firm Louise Piëch and Ferry Porsche founded in 1947, sold in 2011 to Volkswagen AG, which owns it fully.
porscheholdingsalzburg.money: Wholesale and retail of Volkswagen Group brands, financial services and IT systems, with revenue of €25.8 billion in 2022.

porticus.name: Porticus
porticus.what: A philanthropic organisation set up in 1995 to coordinate the giving of the Brenninkmeijer family, owners of C&A, and now part of the family's foundation Constanter.
porticus.money: It raises no funds and advises on grants from Brenninkmeijer family foundations, including Clementia Verein, Stichting Benevolentia, Stiftung Auxilium and Good Energies Foundation.

portomunicipality|Portugal.name: Câmara Municipal do Porto
portomunicipality|Portugal.what: The executive body of the municipality of Porto in Portugal, led by its president, Pedro Duarte.
portomunicipality|Portugal.money: The municipal budget, 491.3 million euros for 2026, raised mainly from local taxes such as the IMI property tax and from fees.

portugueseministryofculture|Portugal.name: Ministério da Cultura, Juventude e Desporto
portugueseministryofculture|Portugal.what: Portugal's government ministry for culture, youth and sport, created in June 2025 by the XXV Constitutional Government; Margarida Balseiro Lopes is minister.

power.name: Power Corporation of Canada
power.what: A Canadian holding company founded in 1925 and based in Montreal, controlled since 1968 by a group led by Paul Desmarais.
power.money: Its financial services holdings in insurance, retirement, wealth and asset management, which have included Great-West Life, Canada Life, IGM Financial and Mackenzie.

praguecityhall|Czech Republic.name: Magistrát hlavního města Prahy
praguecityhall|Czech Republic.what: The administrative office of the City of Prague, formed on 1 January 1922, which carries out tasks set by the City Assembly and City Council from New City Hall.
praguecityhall|Czech Republic.money: The city budget, planned for 2025 with income of CZK 110.92 billion and spending of CZK 113.49 billion.

prefeituradorio.name: Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro
prefeituradorio.what: The municipal government of Rio de Janeiro, led by the mayor and a cabinet of 26 secretariats, with its seat at the Palácio da Cidade.
prefeituradorio.money: The municipal budget of Rio de Janeiro: BRL 45.7 billion in 2024.

preservationleague.name: Preservation League of New York State
preservationleague.what: A non-profit historic preservation organisation founded in 1974 and based in Albany, which gives grants and technical help for historic buildings across New York State.
preservationleague.money: Contributions, 90.3% of its US$1,552,430 revenue in the year to June 2025, with support from the New York State Council on the Arts.
preservationleague.arts: Its Preserve NY Arts + Culture grants, a regrant partnership with the state arts council, pay for building studies of up to US$20,000 for arts and cultural organisations.

princeclaus.name: Prince Claus Fund
princeclaus.what: A Dutch fund set up in 1996 and named after Prince Claus of the Netherlands; it gives grants and awards to artists in places where culture is under pressure.
princeclaus.money: An annual subsidy from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
princeclaus.arts: Its Principal Award is worth €100,000; since 1996 it has supported almost 2,400 projects in 144 countries.

privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.name: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian
privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.what: A Portuguese private foundation in Lisbon, created on 18 July 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, the Armenian oil magnate who settled in Portugal.
privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.
privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.arts: It runs the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum and the Gulbenkian Orchestra, founded in 1962.

privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.name: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.what: A private non-profit contemporary art foundation set up in Turin on 6 April 1995 by the collector Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, its president.
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.money: Mainly public and private contributions: €275,872 public and €1,812,995 private in 2024, of €2,650,394 total revenue.
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.arts: It runs venues in Turin and Guarene d'Alba, a sculpture park at Guarene and the Young Curators Residency Programme.

prohelvetia.name: Pro Helvetia
prohelvetia.what: The Swiss Confederation's arts foundation, set up by the Federal Council in 1939 and made a foundation under public law in 1949; based in Zurich.
prohelvetia.money: The Swiss federal budget, set by parliament in four-year Cultural Messages: CHF 186.9 million for 2025 to 2028.
prohelvetia.arts: In 2025 it approved 2,448 of 7,235 applications and put 86.9 percent of its funds directly into art and culture.

promatrepaulista.name: Pro Matre Paulista
promatrepaulista.what: A private maternity hospital in São Paulo, owned since January 2000 by Grupo Santa Joana, which also runs the Santa Joana and Santa Maria maternity hospitals there.
promatrepaulista.money: Its maternity hospital business within Grupo Santa Joana.

protective.name: Protective Life Corporation
protective.what: A life insurance and annuity holding company in Birmingham, Alabama, whose main subsidiary was founded in 1907, owned since February 2015 by Dai-ichi Life of Tokyo.
protective.money: Sales of life insurance, annuities and asset protection products, with annual revenues of US$7.75 billion.

protesterscitedwilliam.name: The William and Flora Hewlett Foundation
protesterscitedwilliam.what: A private foundation in Menlo Park, California, established in 1966 by William R. Hewlett, co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, and his wife Flora Lamson Hewlett.
protesterscitedwilliam.money: An endowment given by Bill Hewlett and his wife Flora, with assets of approximately $13.9 billion on 31 December 2024.
protesterscitedwilliam.arts: Its Performing Arts Program funds the arts in the San Francisco Bay Area and awarded $40.5 million through 94 grants in 2024.

provinceofbc|Canada.name: Government of British Columbia
provinceofbc|Canada.what: The provincial government of British Columbia, Canada, led by a Premier and Cabinet answerable to the 93-member Legislative Assembly in Victoria.
provinceofbc|Canada.money: Provincial taxes, natural resource royalties and federal transfers; revenue was forecast at C$83.3 billion for 2025-26.

provinceoflimburg|Netherlands.name: Provincie Limburg
provinceoflimburg|Netherlands.what: The government of the Dutch province of Limburg, with a 47-seat provincial council and its seat at the Gouvernement aan de Maas in Maastricht.
provinceoflimburg|Netherlands.money: In 2025 the national provinciefonds paid €284.6 million, its surcharge on motor vehicle tax raised €129.3 million and dividends €22.3 million.

provinceofmanitoba|Canada.name: Government of Manitoba
provinceofmanitoba|Canada.what: The provincial government of Manitoba, Canada: a cabinet led by the premier and drawn from the elected Legislative Assembly, seated in Winnipeg.
provinceofmanitoba|Canada.money: Provincial taxes and federal transfers: Budget 2026 projects C$26,820 million of revenue for 2026/27, including C$9,657 million from the federal government.

provinceofstyriaculturaldepartment|Austr.name: Amt der Steiermärkischen Landesregierung, Abteilung 9 Kultur, Europa, Sport
provinceofstyriaculturaldepartment|Austr.what: Department 9 (Culture, Europe, Sports) of the administration of the Austrian state of Styria, headed by Patrick Schnabl and based at Landhausgasse 7 in Graz.
provinceofstyriaculturaldepartment|Austr.money: The budget of the State of Styria.
provinceofstyriaculturaldepartment|Austr.arts: It publishes a Kulturförderungsbericht each year that sets out how its culture funds were awarded.

provincialcouncilofbiscay|Spain.name: Diputación Foral de Bizkaia
provincialcouncilofbiscay|Spain.what: The governing body of the historical territory of Bizkaia in the Basque Country, headed since 2023 by the diputada general Elixabete Etxanobe.
provincialcouncilofbiscay|Spain.money: The Bizkaia budget: 11,320.3 million euros for 2026, of which 1,716.2 million go to its own departments.
provincialcouncilofbiscay|Spain.arts: Its department of Basque language, culture and sport receives 70.4 million euros in the 2026 budget plan.

provinciezeeland.name: Provincie Zeeland
provinciezeeland.what: The provincial government of Zeeland in the Netherlands, seated in Middelburg, with 39 members in its Provinciale Staten and 394,514 inhabitants at the end of 2025.
provinciezeeland.money: The national provinciefonds, €169.4 million in its 2026 budget, plus €46.3 million from motor vehicle tax surcharges and a €16.0 million Westerscheldetunnel dividend.

prtourism.name: Compañía de Turismo de Puerto Rico
prtourism.what: A government-owned corporation in charge of tourism in Puerto Rico, created under Governor Luis A. Ferré (1969-1973) and headquartered in the former La Princesa jail in San Juan.
prtourism.money: The room occupancy tax on hotel stays, which Act 272 of 2003 moved from the Treasury to the company to levy, collect and distribute.
prtourism.arts: La Princesa also houses a gallery that shows the agency's art collection.
prtourism.address: 2 Paseo de la Princesa, San Juan, PR 00902

psb.name: PJSC Promsvyazbank
psb.what: A Moscow bank founded in 1995, nationalised in 2018, made the supporting bank for Russia's defence industry by a 2019 law and under US and UK sanctions since February 2022.
psb.money: Lending to the defence industry and retail banking: a net loss of RUB 19.2 billion in 2025.

publiccentrefundedbygipuzkoacouncil|Spai.name: Gipuzkoako Foru Aldundia / Diputación Foral de Gipuzkoa
publiccentrefundedbygipuzkoacouncil|Spai.what: The government of the historical territory of Gipuzkoa in the Basque Country, based in San Sebastián and headed by a Diputado General elected by the Juntas Generales.
publiccentrefundedbygipuzkoacouncil|Spai.money: The provincial budget, of which its Hacienda y Finanzas department accounts for about €6.03 billion.

pudilfamily.name: The Pudil Family Foundation
pudilfamily.what: A Czech family foundation in Prague set up by Pavlína Pudil, its board chair, and Petr Pudil; its art collection is on long-term loan to Kunsthalle Praha.
pudilfamily.money: Its co-founder's fortune from a stake in the coal group Czech Coal, sold in 2010, and bpd partners, the family office he co-founded in 2008.
pudilfamily.arts: It supports visual art, research and education and sits on boards and acquisition committees at Tate, KW Berlin and Palais de Tokyo.

puig.name: Puig Brands, S.A.
puig.what: A Spanish fragrance and fashion company founded in Barcelona in 1914 by Antonio Puig Castelló, listed on the Madrid stock exchange and managed by the Puig family.
puig.money: Sales of perfumes, cosmetics and fashion under brands including Carolina Herrera and Charlotte Tilbury, with revenue of €4.3 billion in 2023.

pyur.name: Tele Columbus AG
pyur.what: A Berlin cable network and internet provider, trading as PŸUR since September 2017 and taken over in 2021 by Kublai GmbH, then majority-held by a Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners subsidiary.
pyur.money: Cable television, internet and telephone subscriptions for about three million connected households, with revenue of €422.7 million.

qatarmuseums.name: Qatar Museums
qatarmuseums.what: A Qatari government entity founded in 2005 that runs the country's museums, chaired by Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani under the Amir's patronage.
qatarmuseums.arts: It oversees the Museum of Islamic Art, Mathaf, the National Museum of Qatar and the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum.

qatarshell.name: Qatar Shell
qatarshell.what: Shell's group of companies in Qatar, one of the first international companies to begin oil production there; Richard Tallant chaired it in 2022.
qatarshell.money: Shell's gas business in Qatar, including the Pearl GTL plant at Ras Laffan, run under a production sharing agreement with QatarEnergy.
qatarshell.arts: In November 2018 it agreed to sponsor Company House, the oil history house of Msheireb Museums in Doha.

qattan.name: A. M. Qattan Foundation
qattan.what: A Palestinian non-profit foundation set up in 1993 by the businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah; it is also a registered UK charity.
qattan.money: Donations of £2.02 million and investment income of £484,080 in 2025, of £2.62 million income reported by its UK charity.
qattan.arts: It opened a US$21 million headquarters and arts centre in Ramallah in June 2018.

qattantodate.name: A. M. Qattan Foundation
qattantodate.what: An independent foundation for culture and education in Palestine and the Arab world, set up in 1993 by the Palestinian businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah.
qattantodate.money: Al-Qattan family money: in 2011 the founder put a quarter of his wealth, made through Al-Hani Construction and Trading, into the Al-Qattan Charitable Trust.
qattantodate.arts: It runs the Al-Qattan Cultural Centre in Ramallah, opened in June 2018 at a cost of $21 million, and a cultural centre in Gaza.

qualco.name: Qualco Foundation
qualco.what: A non-profit corporate foundation of Qualco Group, an Athens financial technology company, announced in April 2022 and led by the group's executive chairman Orestis Tsakalotos.
qualco.money: Qualco Group, which sells software, platforms and portfolio management services to banks and financial institutions.
qualco.arts: Culture and Sports is one of its stated pillars of work.

quark.name: Quark Expeditions
quark.what: A polar expedition cruise company with headquarters in Seattle, operating since 1991 in the Arctic and Antarctica, a member of the UK-based Travelopia travel group.
quark.money: Fares for small-ship expedition cruises on ice-class vessels and icebreakers.

rabeesecurities.name: Rabee Securities
rabeesecurities.what: An Iraqi securities brokerage established on 7 January 1995, licensed by the Iraqi Securities Commission and headquartered in Baghdad, chaired by Shwan Ibrahim Taha.
rabeesecurities.money: Brokerage on the Iraq Stock Exchange, investment banking, custody and advisory work; its capital is IQD 3 billion.

rajeebsamdani.name: Samdani Art Foundation
rajeebsamdani.what: A non-profit art trust in Dhaka, founded in 2011 by the collector couple Nadia and Rajeeb Samdani.
rajeebsamdani.money: Rajeeb Samdani is managing director of Golden Harvest Group, a Dhaka conglomerate that also sponsors the Dhaka Art Summit.
rajeebsamdani.arts: It is building Srihatta, an art centre and sculpture park in Sylhet, and gives the Samdani Art Award.

ralesfamily.name: Mitchell P. Rales and Emily Wei Rales
ralesfamily.what: Mitchell Rales co-founded the Danaher Corporation with his brother Steven in 1984 and founded Glenstone with his wife, Emily Wei Rales, in 2006.
ralesfamily.money: Mitchell Rales's fortune from Danaher, Colfax and Fortive, estimated at 4 billion dollars in 2025.
ralesfamily.arts: Mitchell Rales is a former president of the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
ralesfamily.renamed: The atlas name points at the Danaher Corporation, while the museum sentence means a gift from the Rales family.

rattispa.name: Ratti S.p.A. Società Benefit
rattispa.what: An Italian textile company founded in Como in 1945 by Antonio Ratti as Tessitura Serica Antonio Ratti, based in Guanzate and part of the Marzotto Group since 2010.
rattispa.money: Sales of fabrics and accessories to fashion houses.

realdania.name: Realdania
realdania.what: A Danish member-based philanthropic association created in 2000, when Realkredit Danmark sold its mortgage business in its merger with Danske Bank, based in Copenhagen.
realdania.money: Returns on investing the capital it kept from that deal; about 195,000 members own it.
realdania.arts: It funds projects in architecture, planning and the built environment.

recordati.name: Fondazione Hillary Merkus Recordati
recordati.what: A private foundation based in Impruneta near Florence, created by the entrepreneur and art collector Andy Bianchedi in memory of his mother.
recordati.arts: A statutory supporter of Fondazione Palazzo Strozzi since 2024, it appoints one board director and co-promotes the Palazzo Strozzi Future Art programme.
recordati.renamed: The museum sentence means the Fondazione Hillary Merkus Recordati, a private foundation, not Recordati S.p.A., the pharmaceutical company.

regionecampania.name: Regione Campania
regionecampania.what: The regional government of Campania in southern Italy, seated in Naples and led by President Roberto Fico with a 60-member Regional Council.
regionecampania.money: The regional budget, over EUR 38.5 billion for 2026, almost 70% of it for health.
regionecampania.arts: Its 2026 budget raises cinema funding to EUR 6 million and live-performance funding to EUR 17 million.

regionelazio.name: Regione Lazio
regionelazio.what: The regional government of Lazio in central Italy, seated in Rome and led by President Francesco Rocca, with a Regional Council as its legislature.
regionelazio.money: The regional budget; its 2025 economic and financial plan set the 2025 to 2027 budget at about EUR 10 billion.

regionelombardia.name: Regione Lombardia
regionelombardia.what: The regional government of Lombardy, Italy, led by president Attilio Fontana since 2018, with its seat in Milan.

regionepiemonte.name: Regione Piemonte
regionepiemonte.what: The regional government of Piedmont, an Italian region with ordinary statute created in 1948 and operating since 1970; seat in Turin.
regionepiemonte.money: The regional budget, which draws on its own taxes such as IRAP, regional surcharges and car tax.

regions.name: Regions Financial Corporation
regions.what: A bank holding company in Birmingham, Alabama, founded in 1971 as First Alabama Bankshares by the merger of three Alabama banks and renamed in 1994.
regions.money: Commercial, retail and mortgage banking, with revenue of US$9.608 billion and assets of US$158.814 billion in 2025.

regionstockholm|Sweden.name: Region Stockholm
regionstockholm|Sweden.what: The regional public body for Stockholm County, set up on 1 January 2019 in place of Stockholm County Council, running healthcare, public transport and regional planning.
regionstockholm|Sweden.money: The regional budget, about SEK 133 billion in 2024, when the regional income tax rate was 12.38 percent.

relianceindustriesunderbillionairemukesh.name: Reliance Industries Limited
relianceindustriesunderbillionairemukesh.what: An Indian conglomerate founded in 1958 by Dhirubhai Ambani, based in Mumbai and chaired by Mukesh Ambani, with the Ambani family holding 50%.
relianceindustriesunderbillionairemukesh.money: Petroleum refining, petrochemicals, natural gas, retail and telecoms, with revenue of ₹11.04 lakh crore (US$120 billion) in 2026.

republicofkosovoministries|Kosovo.name: Ministria e Kulturës, Rinisë dhe Sportit
republicofkosovoministries|Kosovo.short: Kosovo Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sport
republicofkosovoministries|Kosovo.what: The government ministry of the Republic of Kosovo for culture, youth and sport.
republicofkosovoministries|Kosovo.money: The Kosovo state budget: EUR 86.4 million planned for the ministry in 2025, down from EUR 88.1 million in 2024.

resoluteav.name: Resolute Audio Visual Limited
resoluteav.what: An audio visual and IT installation company trading as Resolute AV, incorporated on 18 October 2023, with its registered office in Godmanchester, Huntingdon.
resoluteav.money: Installing and hiring audio visual systems for commercial, education, residential, church and marine clients.
resoluteav.address: Unit 26 Roman Way Industrial Estate, Roman Way, London Road, Godmanchester, Huntingdon PE29 2LN

rgionbourgognefranchecomt.name: Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.what: The regional council of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, the French region formed on 1 January 2016 from Burgundy and Franche-Comté, seated in Besançon.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.money: A EUR 1.922 billion budget in 2025, led by EUR 699 million of national VAT revenue assigned by the French state.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.arts: Its 2025 budget gives EUR 33.7 million to culture and heritage.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.address: Hôtel de Région, 4 square Castan, 25000 Besançon

rgioncentrevaldeloire.name: Région Centre-Val de Loire
rgioncentrevaldeloire.what: The regional government of Centre-Val de Loire in France, run by an elected regional council of 77 members that sits in Orléans.
rgioncentrevaldeloire.money: The region's own budget, 1.913 billion euros for 2026 before debt rescheduling.

rgiongrandest.name: Région Grand Est
rgiongrandest.what: The regional council of Grand Est, the French region formed in 2016 from Alsace, Champagne-Ardenne and Lorraine, seated in Strasbourg.
rgiongrandest.money: Mostly national VAT shared out by the French state (53% of French regions' operating revenue in 2024); its planned 2026 budget is EUR 4.1 billion.

rgionhautsdefrance.name: Région Hauts-de-France
rgionhautsdefrance.what: The regional government of Hauts-de-France in France, created on 1 January 2016 and run by an elected regional council of 170 members that sits in Lille.
rgionhautsdefrance.money: The region's own budget, 5.2 billion euros for 2026, adopted on 9 April 2026.
rgionhautsdefrance.address: 151 avenue du Président Hoover, 59555 Lille Cedex

rgionledefrance.name: Région Île-de-France
rgionledefrance.what: The French region that contains Paris, run by a regional council of 209 councillors elected for six years, headquartered in Saint-Ouen-sur-Seine.

rgionpaysdelaloire.name: Région Pays de la Loire
rgionpaysdelaloire.what: The regional government of Pays de la Loire in France, run by an elected regional council of 93 members that sits in Nantes.
rgionpaysdelaloire.money: The region's own budget, 1.95 billion euros for 2026.
rgionpaysdelaloire.address: Hôtel de Région, 1 rue de la Loire, 44966 Nantes Cedex 9

rgionsud.name: Région Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
rgionsud.what: The regional council of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, the south-eastern French region also called Région Sud, seated in Marseille.
rgionsud.money: Mainly a share of national VAT assigned by the French state; councillors adopted a EUR 3.2 billion budget for 2024.
rgionsud.arts: The 2024 budget gave EUR 67 million to arts and culture.

rietumubanka.name: Rietumu Banka
rietumubanka.what: A Latvian commercial bank founded on 14 May 1992 with headquarters in Riga, whose largest shareholders are companies of Leonids Esterkins, Dermot Desmond and Arkādijs Suharenko.
rietumubanka.money: Corporate lending and banking services, with assets of €1.5 billion and net profit of €15.9 million in 2023.

rigacity|Latvia.name: Rīgas dome
rigacity|Latvia.what: The government of Riga, Latvia's capital, with 60 councillors elected every four years, meeting in the Town Hall on Rātslaukums.
rigacity|Latvia.money: The city budget: planned revenue of 1.5 billion euros in 2026, with growth from personal income tax, against 1.7 billion euros of spending.
rigacity|Latvia.arts: Its 2026 cultural programme centres on the 825th anniversary of Riga.

right:cohen.name: Steven A. Cohen
right:cohen.what: An American hedge fund manager, founder of Point72 Asset Management (2014, Stamford, Connecticut) and owner of the New York Mets.
right:cohen.money: His hedge fund fortune: S.A.C. Capital Advisors from 1992, which pleaded guilty to insider trading in 2013, then Point72.
right:cohen.arts: The Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation, started in 2001, has granted US$1.5 billion to health, education, arts and culture and New York projects.

rinatmardanov.name: Rinat Mardanov
rinatmardanov.what: A person the atlas names as a backer of the launch of Smena, a contemporary culture centre at Burkhana Shakhidi 7 in Kazan.

ringier.name: Ringier AG
ringier.what: A family-owned Swiss media group dating from the printing press Johann Rudolf Ringier founded in Zofingen in 1833, with offices in Zurich.
ringier.money: Media brands, sports media platforms and digital marketplaces in 18 European and African countries, with revenue of CHF 918.9 million in 2023.
ringier.arts: Over 200 works of contemporary art hang in its offices, an interest of its publisher Michael Ringier.

riodejaneirostate|Brazil.name: Governo do Estado do Rio de Janeiro
riodejaneirostate|Brazil.what: The executive branch of the Brazilian state of Rio de Janeiro, led by the governor, with its seat at the Palácio Guanabara in the state capital since 1975.
riodejaneirostate|Brazil.money: The state budget of Rio de Janeiro.
riodejaneirostate|Brazil.arts: Its culture and creative economy secretariat runs the state culture incentive law, under which ICMS-paying companies put about R$ 230 million into 138 projects in 2024.

rnne.name: Rönne-Stiftung
rnne.what: A non-profit foundation in Berlin, founded in 2020 by Burkhard Saar and named after the Rönnestraße in Charlottenburg, which supports democracy and civil society projects abroad.
rnne.money: A founding endowment from the estate of the Berlin artist and craftsman Ulrich Stroß, plus project grants from the German Federal Foreign Office.

robertdavidliongardiner.name: The Robert David Lion Gardiner Foundation, Inc.
robertdavidliongardiner.what: A private foundation established in 1987 and named for Robert David Lion Gardiner, 16th Lord of the Manor of Gardiner's Island until his death in 2004, based in Riverhead.
robertdavidliongardiner.money: Its endowment, with net assets of US$116,984,003 at December 2025 and income from asset sales, dividends and interest.
robertdavidliongardiner.arts: It funds the study of Long Island history, with grants to historical societies for collections, preservation and exhibition.
robertdavidliongardiner.address: 30 West Main Street, Suite 309, Riverhead, New York 11901

robertsontrust.name: The Robertson Trust
robertsontrust.what: An independent grant-making trust in Glasgow, established in 1961 by the sisters Elspeth, Agnes and Ethel Robertson, who gave it their shares in the family whisky businesses.
robertsontrust.money: Dividends from Edrington, the spirits company behind The Macallan and Highland Park, in which the trust owns all voting shares.
robertsontrust.arts: It has awarded over £300 million across Scotland over 60 years and now directs its funding at poverty and trauma.
robertsontrust.address: Robertson House, 152 Bath Street, Glasgow G2 4TB

robertweilfamily.name: The Robert Weil Family Foundation
robertweilfamily.what: A private foundation in Stockholm established in 2014 by Robert Weil, working in culture, education and democratic engagement.
robertweilfamily.money: Its assets are managed by Proventus AB, the investment company founded in 1969 and owned by Robert Weil and family.
robertweilfamily.arts: It supports fine arts, drama and dance and is a founding patron of Accelerator at Stockholm University, with Magasin III.

rocheespaa.name: Roche Farma, S.A.U.
rocheespaa.what: The Spanish subsidiary of the Swiss healthcare company Roche, constituted in Barcelona on 21 May 1930 and now seated in Madrid.
rocheespaa.money: Sales of medicines and diagnostics in Spain, with net sales of 739.6 million euros in 2024, and Roche Holding owns all its shares.

rockwellautomation.name: Rockwell Automation, Inc.
rockwellautomation.what: A US industrial automation company in Milwaukee, Wisconsin; it began in 1903, founded by Stanton Allen and Lynde Bradley, and took the name Allen-Bradley Company in 1909.
rockwellautomation.money: Sales of industrial automation hardware, software and services under brands such as Allen-Bradley and FactoryTalk: USD 8,342 million in fiscal 2025.

rolex.name: Rolex SA
rolex.what: A Geneva watchmaker founded in London in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf and Alfred Davis, owned since 1960 by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation.
rolex.money: Sales of Rolex and Tudor wristwatches by a company wholly owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, a private Swiss foundation.
rolex.arts: Its Rolex Mentor and Protégé Arts Initiative, set up in 2002, pairs emerging artists with established ones and gives each protégé about $41,000.

rolfhoff.name: Venke and Rolf Hoff
rolfhoff.what: Norwegian art collectors who acquired the KaviarFactory building in Henningsvær, Lofoten, after the cannery closed in 2006 and turned it into a contemporary art space.
rolfhoff.money: Rolf Hoff's business, which makes signage and produces works for artists.
rolfhoff.arts: They have lent works to Tate Britain, Garage in Moscow and most Norwegian contemporary art museums, and support artist-run galleries in Oslo.

romacapitale.name: Roma Capitale
romacapitale.what: The local government of Rome, set up in 2010 under the Italian constitution in place of the comune di Roma, with its seat on the Campidoglio.
romacapitale.money: The municipal budget of Roma Capitale.

romanabramovich.name: Roman Abramovich
romanabramovich.what: A Russian businessman, governor of Chukotka from 2000 to 2008 and former owner of Chelsea football club, sanctioned after the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.
romanabramovich.money: His Sibneft oil stake, sold to the Russian state for $13 billion in 2005, and his Millhouse holdings, which bought 41% of Evraz in 2006.
romanabramovich.arts: He co-founded the Garage Museum of Contemporary Art in Moscow with Dasha Zhukova in 2008.

romantrotsenko.name: Roman Trotsenko
romantrotsenko.what: A Russian businessman born in 1970, owner of the investment company Aeon Corporation and president of United Shipbuilding Corporation from 2009 to 2012.
romantrotsenko.money: 70 percent of Russkaya Energia, which agreed in 2021 to buy the coal miner Vorkutaugol; Forbes put his fortune at USD 1.6 billion in 2019.

rosatommashinostroenie.name: ООО «Росатом Машиностроение»
rosatommashinostroenie.what: The machine building division of Rosatom, the Russian state nuclear corporation, whose factories make reactor equipment for power plants and nuclear icebreakers.
rosatommashinostroenie.money: Sales of equipment for nuclear and thermal power plants, made in Moscow, St Petersburg, Karelia and the Moscow, Rostov, Nizhny Novgorod and Yekaterinburg regions.

rosenthalfamily.name: Rosenthal Family Foundation
rosenthalfamily.what: A private family foundation in Cincinnati, set up in 1986 by Lois and Richard Rosenthal, owners of the publisher F&W Publications.
rosenthalfamily.money: The Rosenthals' money from F&W Publications, sold in December 1999, with net assets of $27,719,722 at the end of 2024.
rosenthalfamily.arts: In 1999 it gave $6 million toward the Contemporary Arts Center building in Cincinnati, which carries the Rosenthals' name.

rotasa.name: Rotasa Foundation
rotasa.what: A private family foundation in Redwood City, California, with Rose Webb Roven as president and Susan Cummins as secretary, whose last listed tax return covers the year to June 2017.
rotasa.money: Contributions received each year: $557,162 of its $760,672 revenue in the year to June 2016.

royalairmaroc.name: Royal Air Maroc
royalairmaroc.what: Morocco's national airline, founded in July 1953 and headquartered at Casablanca-Anfa Airport, with the Moroccan state holding about 98% of its capital.
royalairmaroc.money: Passenger and cargo flights, with revenue of 19.7 billion Moroccan dirhams in 2023.

royalinstituteofbritisharchitects.name: Royal Institute of British Architects
royalinstituteofbritisharchitects.what: The professional membership body for architects in the United Kingdom, formed in 1834, incorporated by Royal Charter and registered as a charity, with headquarters in London.
royalinstituteofbritisharchitects.money: Charitable activities (£17.61 million), investments (£9.37 million) and trading (£4.68 million) made up most of its £32,357,000 income in 2025.

royalnorwegianembassy|Tanzania.name: Royal Norwegian Embassy in Dar es Salaam
royalnorwegianembassy|Tanzania.what: Norway's embassy in Tanzania, a mission of the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dar es Salaam that also represents Norway in Burundi, Comoros, Rwanda and Uganda.
royalnorwegianembassy|Tanzania.money: The Norwegian government through its foreign ministry, and the embassy signed a NOK 19 million grant to the Legal and Human Rights Centre in 2025.
royalnorwegianembassy|Tanzania.address: Cnr. Garden Avenue/Mirambo Street, Dar es Salaam

rtx.name: RTX Corporation
rtx.what: A US aerospace and defence group formed in 2020 by merging Raytheon with the aerospace businesses of United Technologies; its units are Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon.
rtx.money: Aircraft engines, avionics, guided missiles and air defence systems: revenue of USD 88.6 billion in 2025, 38 percent of it from the US government.

rubelli.name: Rubelli S.p.A.
rubelli.what: A Venetian silk and furnishing textile company dating to Lorenzo Rubelli's purchase of the G.B. Trapolin weaving mill in 1889; Alessandro Favaretto Rubelli is its president.
rubelli.money: Sales of silk fabrics and furnishing textiles worldwide.
rubelli.arts: It set up the Rubelli Foundation in 2018 to safeguard its textile heritage, and has given to the Fondazione Giorgio Cini, Venetian Heritage and Save Venice.

rubismcnat.name: Rubis Mécénat
rubismcnat.what: The endowment fund of the French energy group Rubis, running artistic and social projects since 2011.
rubismcnat.money: The Rubis group, founded in 1990 by Gilles Gobin in Paris, which stores and distributes petroleum products and LPG.
rubismcnat.arts: It funds the Prix Rubis Mécénat with the Beaux-Arts de Paris and youth programmes in South Africa, Madagascar and Jamaica.

rundirectlybyrgionoccitanie.name: Région Occitanie / Pyrénées-Méditerranée
rundirectlybyrgionoccitanie.what: The regional council of Occitanie in France, created on 1 January 2016 by merging the Languedoc-Roussillon and Midi-Pyrénées councils, with 158 councillors and its seat in Toulouse.
rundirectlybyrgionoccitanie.money: The regional budget voted by its councillors, 3.54 billion euros for 2026.

russianfederalstate|Russia.name: Министерство культуры Российской Федерации
russianfederalstate|Russia.what: The Russian federal ministry for culture policy, formed on 2 May 2008 and led by Olga Lyubimova since 21 January 2020; the Hermitage is in its charge.
russianfederalstate|Russia.money: The federal budget of Russia, which pays federal museums such as the Hermitage subsidies for their state assignments.

russianstate|Italy.name: Российская Федерация
russianstate|Italy.what: The Russian federal state, whose government owns Russia’s national pavilion in the Giardini of the Venice Biennale, as each national pavilion there belongs to its government.
russianstate|Italy.wrong_match: The pavilion’s line names the Russian state only as owner of the building, and Novatek, not the state, paid for the 2021 renovation.

russianstate|Russia.name: Министерство культуры Российской Федерации
russianstate|Russia.what: The Russian federal ministry for culture policy, formed on 2 May 2008 and led by Olga Lyubimova since 21 January 2020; the State Russian Museum is in its charge.
russianstate|Russia.money: The federal budget of the Russian Federation.

russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.name: Leonid Mikhelson
russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.what: A Russian businessman, born in 1955, who is chairman, chief executive and major shareholder of the gas company Novatek; he set up the V-A-C Foundation in 2009.

saastamoinen.name: Saastamoisen säätiö sr

safraeach.name: Edmond J. Safra Philanthropic Foundation

saintgobain20.name: Compagnie de Saint-Gobain S.A.

turing.money: Proceeds of the stock exchange listing of TomTom, which Pieter Geelen co-founded in 1991 as the Turing Machine Company.

uccsubvention.name: University College Cork
uccsubvention.what: A public university in Cork, Ireland, founded in 1845 as one of three Queen's Colleges and now a constituent university of the National University of Ireland.
uccsubvention.money: Revenue of €572.4 million in 2024/25: academic fees €181.96 million, research grants and contracts €131.87 million, State grants €100.12 million.

udoundanettebrandhorst.name: Udo und Anette Brandhorst Stiftung
udoundanettebrandhorst.what: A Munich foundation set up in 1993 by the collectors Udo and Anette Brandhorst; its 1999 agreement with the Free State of Bavaria led to the Museum Brandhorst.
udoundanettebrandhorst.money: An endowment of €120 million in 2009; Anette Brandhorst was a great-granddaughter of the founder of Henkel.

ukgovernment|UK.name: His Majesty's Government
ukgovernment|UK.what: The central executive of the United Kingdom, led by Prime Minister Andy Burnham since 20 July 2026, whose ministers answer to Parliament.

ukresearch.name: UK Research and Innovation
ukresearch.what: A non-departmental public body of the UK government, launched in April 2018 under the Higher Education and Research Act 2017, joining seven research councils, Research England and Innovate UK.
ukresearch.money: The science budget of its sponsor, the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.

ulsteruniversity.name: Ulster University
ulsteruniversity.what: A public university in Northern Ireland, legally the University of Ulster, formed in 1984 by merging the New University of Ulster and Ulster Polytechnic; its legal address is in Coleraine.
ulsteruniversity.money: Its budget was £304.4 million in 2024/25; in June 2023 the Government of Ireland announced about €45 million in funding for it.

umicore.name: Umicore
umicore.what: A Belgian materials technology company headquartered in Brussels, formed in 1989 by a merger of four mining and smelting companies and known as Union Minière before 2001.
umicore.money: Recycling and refining of precious metals, automotive catalysts and battery materials; revenue was €3.6 billion in 2025.

unam.name: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México
unam.what: Mexico's national public research university, founded in its modern form on 22 September 1910 by Justo Sierra, with its main campus at Ciudad Universitaria in Mexico City.
unam.money: Federal subsidy: MXN 53,749 million of its MXN 59,878 million budget for 2026, with own income making up the rest.
unam.arts: It runs 26 museums and 18 historic sites.

undernonprofitmill6.name: MILL6 Foundation
undernonprofitmill6.what: A non-profit arts and cultural organisation founded in 2015 that manages and operates CHAT (Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile) at The Mills in Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong.

undp.name: United Nations Development Programme
undp.what: The United Nations agency for development aid, founded on 22 November 1965 and based at UN headquarters in New York, with offices in 177 countries.
undp.money: Voluntary contributions from UN member states; its budget for 2026 was US$6,482.63 million as of August 2026.

unesco.name: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
unesco.what: A specialised agency of the United Nations founded in 1945, with 194 member states and headquarters in Paris.
unesco.money: Assessed contributions that member states must pay, plus voluntary contributions from governments, international bodies, companies and other donors.

unicredit.name: UniCredit S.p.A.

unicredit.money: Its banking business: revenue of EUR 24.844 billion in 2024.

unicreditbank.name: UniCredit Bank S.A.
unicreditbank.what: A Romanian bank in the UniCredit Group, formed when Ion Țiriac Bank, founded in 1991, merged with HVB Bank Romania in June 2005; named UniCredit Bank since August 2015.
unicreditbank.money: Banking for individuals, small firms and companies through 208 branches; total assets were RON 34.6 billion at the end of 2015.

unipar.name: Unipar Carbocloro S.A.

unipar.money: Sales of chlorine, caustic soda and PVC from plants in Cubatão and Santo André in Brazil and Bahía Blanca in Argentina.

unipol.name: Unipol Assicurazioni S.p.A.

unipol.money: Insurance sold under brands such as UniSalute and Linear; its largest shareholder was Coop Alleanza 3.0 with 23.48% in June 2025.

uniqa.name: UNIQA Insurance Group AG

uniqlo.name: Fast Retailing Co., Ltd.

unitedperformingarts.name: United Performing Arts Fund

unitedperformingarts.money: Gifts from individuals, companies and foundations, with no government funding: contributions were 96.4 percent of its $8.25 million revenue in the year to August 2025.

universitymuseumofumeuniversity.name: Umeå universitet

universityofchile.name: Universidad de Chile
universityofchile.what: A public university in Santiago, founded by the Chilean state on 19 November 1842 under the government of Manuel Bulnes, with 40,494 students.

universityofmelbourne.name: The University of Melbourne
universityofmelbourne.what: A public research university established by an act of the Parliament of Victoria on 22 January 1853, with its main campus in Parkville, Melbourne.

universityofpennsylvaniaculturalpartners.name: University of Pennsylvania

universityofsouthampton.money: Income of £737.6 million in 2024/25, of which £141.4 million came from research grants and contracts.

universityofwitwatersrand.name: University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg

uruguaysministryofeducation|Uruguay.name: Ministerio de Educación y Cultura
uruguaysministryofeducation|Uruguay.what: Uruguay's government ministry for education policy, cultural development, heritage, science and human rights, in Montevideo.

uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.name: Friends of the Ixchel Museum Inc

usfincaviga.name: Finca Vigía Foundation
usfincaviga.what: A US nonprofit in Boston founded in 2002 by Jenny and Frank Phillips to restore Ernest Hemingway's house and papers at Finca Vigía, Cuba.

uwebristol.name: University of the West of England, Bristol

valeculturalinstitute.name: Instituto Cultural Vale

vancleef.name: Van Cleef & Arpels

veinisober.name: Veinisõber

verenigingehbk.name: Vereniging Eerste Hulp Bij Kunst

victorpinchuk.name: Victor Pinchuk Foundation

vikingcruises.name: Viking Holdings Ltd

villasandi.name: Villa Sandi

villedestrasbourg|France.name: Ville de Strasbourg

weenergies.name: We Energies Foundation
weenergies.what: The corporate foundation of We Energies, the Wisconsin electricity and gas utility of WEC Energy Group in Milwaukee, tax-exempt since May 1983.
weenergies.money: The stockholders of WEC Energy Group fund it; the group sells electricity and natural gas to 4.4 million customers in four states.

weilfamilyofficeproventus.name: Proventus AB
weilfamilyofficeproventus.what: A family-owned investment company in Stockholm, founded in 1969 and owned by Robert Weil and family, organised since 2017 as a family office.
weilfamilyofficeproventus.money: Returns on the Weil family's assets, invested in equities, fixed income, currencies and alternatives.
weilfamilyofficeproventus.arts: It manages the assets of the Robert Weil Family Foundation, which continues the culture work Robert Weil earlier ran through the company.

weitzerhotels.name: Florian Weitzer Holding GmbH
weitzerhotels.what: A family-owned hotel and restaurant group trading as Florian Weitzer Hotels & Restaurants, whose Hotel Weitzer in Graz has belonged to the Weitzer family since 1910.
weitzerhotels.money: Income from its hotels and restaurants in Graz, Vienna, Salzburg and Semmering, among them Hotel Daniel, Grand Hôtel Wiesler and Grand Ferdinand.

wellcometrustendowment.name: Wellcome Trust
wellcometrustendowment.what: A charitable foundation for health research based in London, founded in 1936 under the will of the pharmaceutical entrepreneur Sir Henry Wellcome.
wellcometrustendowment.money: Returns on an investment portfolio of £39.9 billion, built from Henry Wellcome's fortune in the drug company Burroughs Wellcome.
wellcometrustendowment.arts: The Wellcome Building at 183 Euston Road houses Wellcome Collection; the Trust spent £1.1 billion on charitable activities in 2023/24.
wellcometrustendowment.address: Gibbs Building, 215 Euston Road, London NW1 2BE

wellingtoncitycouncil|New Zealand.name: Wellington City Council

wellingtoncitycouncil|New Zealand.money: Rates collected from Wellington property owners, which rose by an average of 12 percent in its 2025/26 budget.
wellingtoncitycouncil|New Zealand.arts: Its Arts and Culture Multi-Year Funding pays organisations a yearly amount, generally in three-year cycles, under its Aho Tini arts policy.

wesfarmersarts.name: Wesfarmers Limited
wesfarmersarts.what: An Australian conglomerate headquartered in Perth, with retail, chemicals, fertiliser, industrial and safety businesses, mainly in Australia and New Zealand.
wesfarmersarts.money: Sales of its businesses, with revenue of A$45.7 billion in the 2025 financial year.
wesfarmersarts.arts: Wesfarmers Arts funds arts groups in Western Australia and nationally and manages the Wesfarmers Collection of Australian Art.
wesfarmersarts.address: Level 14, Brookfield Place Tower 2, 123 St Georges Terrace, Perth WA 6000

westernfrontat.name: Western Front Foundation
westernfrontat.what: A society of artists and long-term patrons affiliated with the Vancouver artist-run centre Western Front, which set up the Western Front Endowment Fund in 2003.

westernpennsylvaniaconservancy.name: Western Pennsylvania Conservancy
westernpennsylvaniaconservancy.what: A private nonprofit conservation organisation founded in 1932 and headquartered in Pittsburgh, which Edgar Kaufmann Jr. entrusted with Fallingwater in 1963.
westernpennsylvaniaconservancy.money: Gifts from its members and other income, with total revenue of $32,834,272 and total assets of $139,538,974 in 2024.

wexnercenter.name: Wexner Center Foundation
wexnercenter.what: A nonprofit in Columbus, Ohio, tax-exempt since 1990, that supports Ohio State University's Wexner Center for the Arts; Leslie H. Wexner, founder of Limited Brands, chairs its trustees.

whanki.name: Whanki Foundation
whanki.what: A foundation that Kim Hyang-an, the painter Kim Whanki's widow, founded in New York in 1979 and moved to Seoul in 1989; it opened the Whanki Museum in 1992.

whitecube.name: White Cube
whitecube.what: A contemporary art gallery established in London in 1993 by the art dealer Jay Jopling, who owns it, with galleries in London, Hong Kong, New York, Paris and Seoul.
whitecube.money: Sales of work by the more than 70 artists and artist estates it represents.

wienerberger.name: Wienerberger AG
wienerberger.what: An Austrian building materials group founded in Vienna in 1819, the world's largest producer of bricks, listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange with all shares in free float.
wienerberger.money: Sales of bricks, roof tiles, pavers and pipe systems from more than 200 plants in 28 countries, with revenue of €4,566 million in 2025.
wienerberger.arts: It runs the Brick Award for clay and brick architecture.

wienerstdtische.name: Wiener Städtische Versicherung AG
wienerstdtische.what: An Austrian insurer founded in Vienna in 1824, the largest single company in the Vienna Insurance Group.
wienerstdtische.money: Insurance premiums, about EUR 3,196.2 million gross; the Wiener Städtische Versicherungsverein is the group's main shareholder.

williampenn.name: William Penn Foundation
williampenn.what: A private grant-making foundation in Philadelphia, founded in 1945 as the Phoebe Waterman Foundation by Otto Haas, co-founder of the chemical company Rohm and Haas, and his wife Phoebe.
williampenn.money: Much of the estate of Otto Haas, who ran Rohm and Haas until his death in 1960, with net assets of $3.3 billion in 2024.

winnipegartscouncil|Canada.name: Winnipeg Arts Council
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.what: A not-for-profit charity that the City of Winnipeg charges with distributing its arts funding and managing its Public Art Policy.
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.money: City arts funding of C$4.65 million in 2025, plus C$258,570 for five city-designated museums.

wirth.name: Hauser & Wirth AG
wirth.what: A commercial gallery for modern and contemporary art, founded in Zurich in 1992 by Iwan Wirth, Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser, with galleries in Europe, Asia and North America.

wissam.name: Wissam Nesr
wissam.what: Chief executive of Webcor Group, a food importer and distributor that is one of the largest companies in Angola, and co-founder with his wife Hiba of the Nesr Art Foundation.

wolfson.name: The Wolfson Foundation
wolfson.what: A UK grant-making charity set up in 1955 by Isaac Wolfson, chairman of Great Universal Stores, with his wife and son Leonard; based in London.
wolfson.money: Its endowment, just under £1 billion in 2024, when it spent £44 million on charitable activities.

workerspartyofkorea.name: Workers' Party of Korea
workerspartyofkorea.what: The ruling party of North Korea, founded in 1949 from a merger of the Workers' Parties of North and South Korea, led by General Secretary Kim Jong Un.
workerspartyofkorea.money: Its Central Committee Bureau 39 (Room 39) keeps a foreign currency fund for North Korea's leaders.

wrth.name: Würth Group
wrth.what: A family-owned German group selling fastening and assembly materials, founded by Adolf Würth in Künzelsau in 1945 and led by his son Reinhold Würth from 1954.

wstenrot.name: Wüstenrot Stiftung Gemeinschaft der Freunde Deutscher Eigenheimverein e.V.

wstenrotjoinedrestoration.name: Wüstenrot Stiftung Gemeinschaft der Freunde Deutscher Eigenheimverein e.V.

wstenrotjoinedrestoration.money: Two holding companies that own 40% and 26% of Wüstenrot & Württembergische AG, the listed building society and insurance group in Kornwestheim.
wstenrotjoinedrestoration.arts: Its monuments programme repairs and researches listed buildings such as the Einstein Tower in Potsdam and the Chancellor's Bungalow in Bonn, with a focus on heritage built after 1945.

xacbank.name: XacBank

xcelenergy.name: Xcel Energy Inc.
xcelenergy.what: A listed electricity and natural gas utility based in Minneapolis, built on Northern States Power, Public Service Company of Colorado and Southwestern Public Service, with origins in 1909.
xcelenergy.money: Electricity sold to about 3.9 million customers and natural gas to 2.2 million across eight states, with revenue of $13.44 billion in 2024.
xcelenergy.arts: The Xcel Energy Foundation gave $4.6 million in grants to 390 nonprofit organisations in 2024, in STEM career pathways, community vitality and environmental sustainability.

yakovmargulis.name: Yakov Margulis
yakovmargulis.what: A Kazan businessman, paediatrician by training and former head of Tattekhmedfarm, who owns the building at Burkhana Shakhidi 7 that houses the Smena centre.
yakovmargulis.wrong_match: He is Smena's landlord: the line and Business Online (16 April 2016) show low rent in his building, not money given.

yandexeda.name: Yandex.Eda LLC

yayasanilham.name: Yayasan ILHAM

yokohamacitymanagementfee|Japan.name: City of Yokohama

yoosungyeon.name: Yoo Sung-yeon

zabludowiczarttrust.name: Zabludowicz Art Trust

zeitzmocaa.name: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa

zentrumpaulkleemauricee.name: Zentrum Paul Klee - Maurice E. and Martha Müller Foundation

zionsbank.name: Zions Bancorporation, N.A.

zumtobel.name: Zumtobel Group AG

zwirner.name: David Zwirner

zwirner.money: Sales of works by the more than seventy artists and estates it represents, in the primary and secondary art markets.
